Abstract: We present the first dedicated $v\sin i$ survey of blue straggler stars (BSS) in the old open cluster Collinder 261 ($t=6.7$ Gyr), based on VLT/FLAMES-GIRAFFE spectroscopy of 40 BSS and 42 turn-off/subgiant (TO/SGB) reference stars. Seventeen of the 39 BSS entering the statistics (44%) rotate faster than 40 km/s, whereas all TO/SGB reference stars are slow rotators; fast rotation is strongly linked to spectroscopic binarity. TESS light curves identify seven eclipsing or ellipsoidal binaries with $P_{orb}=0.5$-2.1 d, all rotating at the velocity set by tidal synchronisation, so in these systems the fast rotation is maintained by a close post-mass-transfer orbit and does not date the formation event. Differential C, O, Ba, and Fe abundances for the 22 slow rotators reveal that 62% carry the surface-pollution signature of mass transfer, in two distinct patterns separated by an empty ~1 dex gap in [Ba/Fe]: a Ba-rich group tracing AGB donors and a C/O-enhanced, Ba-normal group tracing donors below the $s$-process activation mass. The BSS iron abundance is consistent with the cluster value; the few apparent Fe excesses are partly explained by differential reddening and do not affect the abundance pattern. The correlated C-O enrichment is opposite to the depletion seen in globular-cluster BSS, indicating binaries wide enough for donors to reach the AGB. With $A^+_{r_h}=0.171\pm0.034$ and $f_{FR-BSS}=44\pm8$%, Collinder 261 extends the globular-cluster rotation-density trends into the open-cluster regime: its BSS were assembled by a continuously operating binary channel, and their chemistry records the dynamical environment of the host cluster.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13128.title: Planetary material is a major source of hydrogen in helium-atmosphere white dwarfs
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13128.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13128v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many white dwarfs with helium-dominated atmospheres show traces of hydrogen in their spectra. On average, the total mass of hydrogen within their convective envelopes increases with age, but there is no consensus on the origin of such hydrogen. Hypotheses include upward diffusion from hidden reservoirs deep within the envelope, or accretion, alongside heavier elements, of planetary material. We construct a simple model that includes both pathways, and test it using two independent samples of helium-atmosphere DB white dwarfs from the DESI and SDSS spectroscopic surveys, selected to have Gaia colours BP-RP > -0.25, corresponding roughly to 10000 < $T_{\rm eff}$ < 19000K. We find that at least $22 \pm 2$ per cent of the helium-atmosphere white dwarfs with detectable hydrogen must have accreted some of it from their planetary systems, via ices, hydrated minerals or atmospheres. We thus demonstrate that planetary hydrogen is a necessary ingredient to explain the spectral evolution of white dwarfs as a population, rather than only extreme hydrogen-enriched cases.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13132.title: Searching for Planets around Altair with JWST/NIRcam
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13132.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13132v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Altair (alpha Aql) is one of the nearest stars to the Sun at 5.13 pc and its age has recently been revised to 88+/-10 Myr, making it one of the youngest stars in the Solar neighborhood. This makes Altair a compelling target for high-contrast direct imaging searches for giant planets. We present two epochs of simultaneous F444W and F200W MASK430R JWST/NIRCam coronagraphic imaging observations. After post-processing, these data achieve F444W contrast levels of 2 x 10^-6 at 1" (5.1 au), 1.5 x 10^-7 at 2" (10.3 au), and a few x 10^-8 beyond 4"(20 au). Using the Sonora Flame Skimmer models, this corresponds to sub-Jupiter mass sensitivity beyond 5 au and sub-Saturn mass sensitivity beyond 10 au. We identified several candidate point sources in the field in the first epoch data. Second epoch observations confirmed that none of the candidates were co-moving with Altair and their colors are consistent with background stars. Altair has no known companions, no detected debris disk, and is not associated with any stellar association. Despite this, its youth and proximity ensure it will remain a high-priority target for future high-contrast imaging observations. We additionally discuss Altair as a potential reference star for future observations, presenting measurements of background sources in the field and showing that Altair will remain at least a few arcsec from background stars over the next 10-20 years, making it a reliable reference target for upcoming imaging campaigns including the Roman Space Telescope Coronagraph Instrument.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13136.title: Near-Ultraviolet and Optical Observations of the White Dwarf ZTF J0328$-$1219 Reveal Variable Periodicity in its Transiting Debris System
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13136.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13136v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We observed the transiting debris disk system around the white dwarf ZTF J0328$-$1219 using the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) in 2025 October, obtaining near-ultraviolet (NUV) spectroscopy with STIS over five consecutive HST orbits. Our abundance analysis supports the accretion of a chondritic body. We complemented our HST program with 16 days of optical time-series photometry beginning in 2025 October, which reveal variable periodicity and rapidly evolving transit morphology. Previous monitoring by TESS during Sectors 4 and 31 confirmed a predominant, stable transit orbital period, $P_{\rm A} = 9.937$ hr, along with a second, transient period, $P_{\rm B} = 11.2$ hr. Our 2025 autumn light curves show transits are dominated by $P_{\rm B} = 11.17$ hr with $P_{\rm A}$ initially appearing as a weaker, secondary feature and eventually returning to predominance. We also identify a candidate transit period of 7.64 hr during the final days of the 2025 autumn campaign, although its significance and persistence remain uncertain. We add simultaneous $ugr$ light curves collected with ULTRACAM in 2024 November that are dominated by $P_{\rm A}$ and show no significant color term. We further compare the transit depths in optical photometry concurrent with our NUV observations, again measuring a lack of transit-dependent extinction except during the fifth HST orbit where a reddening term may arise. The observed variable periodicity and potentially changing color behavior illuminate ongoing dynamical processes, namely collisions, and demonstrate the opportunity for studying dust physics in real time at white dwarf debris disks.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13147.title: Identification of chromospheric dynamical signatures in the 2022 December 27 solar flare with DKIST
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13147.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13147v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spectroscopic observations by the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST) with unprecedented capabilities provide new insights into the evolving fine structure in the chromosphere during solar flares. We analyzed Ca II 8542\r{A} spectra, formed in the middle chromosphere, of a minor flare observed by DKIST's Visible Spectropolarimeter in a single raster lasting 1.5 hours. We characterized the dynamic features in the spectra, then identified the spatial scales and context of these features during the evolution of flare heating. To do so, we developed a multi-layer, hierarchical clustering algorithm, with which 17,422 line profiles of flaring spectra were characterized into 19 clusters of similar spectral features. We then examined the spatial structure of the spectral clusters and also the time when the spectra were observed with respect to the local heating history inferred from observations by the Atmosphere Imaging Assembly. The spectral clusters form a set of spatially coherent structures, comprised of a central kernel with an enveloping halo. The smallest kernel size that is identified has a width of $\le 400$ km. Furthermore, spectral clusters in the pore and plage exhibit distinct properties such as kernel size, line shift, and spatial variation, which may be a result of different background atmosphere, and may also reflect different stage of local heating. High-resolution observations with improved cadence can further our understanding of the evolution of chromospheric fine structure.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13181.title: Dust Reverberation Mapping of Low-Mass Active Galactic Nuclei
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13181.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13181v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We perform a systematic dust reverberation mapping study of low-mass ($M_{\mathrm{BH}}\sim10^6$-$10^7 M_\odot$) active galactic nuclei (AGNs) selected from a literature-compiled catalog, using data from the Zwicky Transient Facility and the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer. Through quality assessments, we obtain a core sample of 65 sources with W1- and W2-band lag measurements relative to optical light curves. The W2-band lags are generally longer than the W1-band lags, with a median ratio of $\tau_{\mathrm{W2}}/\tau_{\mathrm{W1}}=1.24^{+0.33}_{-0.21}$. We further investigate the relations between dust radius and AGN luminosity ($R_{\mathrm{dust}}-L_{\mathrm{AGN}}$), using different lag measurements and luminosity proxies. Combining our sample with a higher-luminosity AGN sample, we establish unified $R_{\mathrm{dust}}-L_{\mathrm{AGN}}$ relations spanning nearly seven orders of magnitude in bolometric luminosity. The slopes are $0.47\pm0.01$ and $0.44\pm0.01$ for the W1 and W2 bands, slightly below the expectation of $0.5$ from dust radiative equilibrium. In the combined sample, the lag deviations show a negative correlation with Eddington ratio, potentially related to the self-shadowing effect of slim disks. The luminosity-dependent SED variations revealed by the SPHEREx composite spectra suggest that individual luminosity proxies may not fully trace the intrinsic dust-heating luminosity. Both effects may contribute to the shallow $R_{\mathrm{dust}}-L_{\mathrm{AGN}}$ slopes. Future joint optical and near-infrared monitoring with the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will further extend dust RM studies to lower-luminosity AGNs hosting lower-mass black holes.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13185.title: Giant Radio Galaxies from the Third Data Release of the LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey (LoTSS-DR3): Physical Characteristics and Environments
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13185.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13185v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Giant radio galaxies (GRGs) are radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGN) with projected linear sizes exceeding 0.7 Mpc, offering insights into the evolution of large-scale radio jets and their environments. We present 2333 GRGs from the LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey Data Release 3 (LoTSS-DR3), with projected sizes of 0.7-2.9 Mpc, redshifts of $0.126 \leq z \leq 3.517$, and 150-MHz radio luminosities of $1.72 \times 10^{24}$-$3.04 \times 10^{28}$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Of these, 726 ($\sim 31\%$) lie at $z \geq 1$. We investigate their radio properties, lobe energetics, equipartition pressures, black hole masses, mid-infrared colours, and environments. Equipartition pressure decreases with increasing projected size, consistent with declining lobe energy density as radio structures expand, while its positive correlation with redshift persists after controlling for radio power and projected size. WISE colours highlight the diversity of the host-galaxy population, with approximately 75% of sources with available photometry falling within the empirical AGN/HERG region. For BCG-hosted GRGs, physical projected size shows no significant dependence on cluster mass. Although the normalized projected half-size, $D/(2r_{500})$, decreases with increasing cluster mass, this trend is consistent with the expected self-similar scaling of cluster radius rather than an independent suppression of radio-source growth in massive clusters. The substantial high-redshift population provides an opportunity to investigate GRGs at early cosmic epochs, although surface-brightness dimming and inverse-Compton losses against the cosmic microwave background can limit their detectability.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13195.title: TITAN DR1: The Type Ia Supernova Trove from ATLAS in the Nearby Universe - Host Galaxies I: Associations, Redshifts and Derived Properties
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13195.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13195v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present the host-galaxy catalogue for TITAN DR1, a sample of 8378 spectroscopically confirmed Type Ia supernovae (SNe~Ia) at $z \lesssim 0.15$ -- the largest homogeneous low-redshift SN Ia sample assembled to date. We describe the association of each SN with its host, the compilation of redshifts, measurements of uniform far-ultraviolet to mid-infrared (FUV--MIR) photometry, and the derivation of host properties through spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting. Combining four host-association methods with manual vetting, we securely identify hosts for 7856 SNe~Ia (93.8\%). We compile host-galaxy spectroscopic redshifts for 5522 objects and provide CMB-frame and peculiar-velocity-corrected redshifts. \rev{PSF-matched} photometry is measured for 7568 host galaxies, including both global fluxes and local optical-only fluxes within a fixed 1.5~kpc aperture centred on the SN; \texttt{Bagpipes} returns successful global fits for \rev{all} hosts and local fits for 7329. Stellar mass and rest-frame $g-z$ colour are robustly measured from optical data alone, whereas reliable estimates of star-formation rate, dust attenuation, and mass-weighted age require broader wavelength coverage to break age--dust degeneracies\rev{, and are reported for 5827 hosts}; in our redshift range, MIR data suffice and far-IR coverage is not required. The hosts span a representative low-redshift galaxy population, with a median stellar mass of $\log_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)=10.22$ (\rev{60\%} high-mass; $\log_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)>10$), \rev{71\%} star-forming ($\log_{10}(\mathrm{sSFR}/\mathrm{yr}^{-1}) > -10.5$), and an approximately exponential $A_V$ distribution. This catalogue provides the foundation for forthcoming analyses of the luminosity step and the broader role of galaxy environment in SN~Ia standardization and cosmology.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13225.title: Intermediate-redshift slow rotators as the progenitors of the most massive galaxies at z $\sim$ 0
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13225.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13225v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the resolved stellar kinematics and star formation histories, and their dependence on the environment, in a sample of 218 intermediate redshift (0.1 < z < 1) galaxies located in the CANDELS and COSMOS fields, observed with VLT/MUSE. The sample covers galaxies with stellar masses ranging M_star ~10^8 - 10^12 M_sun, including both star-forming and quiescent systems. For 113 galaxies, found in dense environments of galaxy groups, we derive the spin parameter ($\lambda_{R}$), while for the rest of the sample, we use data from previous papers in this series. Given that the surveys used in this work are flux-limited, the $\lambda_{R}$ distribution of our full sample lacks the bimodality observed in the local Universe, but the subsample of galaxies at z < 0.6 resembles the galaxy population in the nearby Universe, in terms of mass, sizes, and stellar population properties, more than galaxies at z > 0.6. We classified the galaxies into fast and slow rotators, finding that ~8% (17/218) of the galaxies are slow-rotating. The fraction of slow rotators does not change significantly down to z = 0, but we find that in the z ~ 0 sample, the spin parameter is, on average, higher than at higher redshifts. In our subsample at z > 0.6, we observed evidence for the existence of the kinematic morphology-density relation. The slow rotators in our sample mostly assemble their stellar mass in one or two main episodes of formation, and they finished assembling their mass via star formation by redshift of z $\sim$ 1. It is however, not clear if the loss of angular momentum can be associated with the last star formation episode. Based on their location in the mass - size diagram, the intermediate-redshift galaxies are consistent with being the progenitors of the most massive slow rotators observed at z~0, where the subsequent growth is facilitated through gas-poor (dry) mergers.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13247.title: Detectability of Seyfert galaxies in point-source and stacking searches with a global network of neutrino telescopes
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13247.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13247v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent evidence for high-energy neutrino emission from NGC 1068 and other nearby Seyfert galaxies suggests that active galactic nuclei (AGNs) may constitute a class of astrophysical neutrino sources. Using a physically motivated neutrino emission model based on stochastic particle acceleration in magnetized AGN coronae, we investigate the detection prospects of X-ray-bright Seyfert galaxies with a detector network comprising IceCube, Baikal-GVD, KM3NeT/ARCA, and P-ONE. We find that the Circinus Galaxy is the most promising point-source target in the Southern sky and will be detected at the 5$\sigma$ level by 2038 at the latest, provided that the Seyfert population accounts for the diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux up to 100 TeV and Circinus is at least as efficient a neutrino emitter as the average source in the population. Individual detections of other nearby Seyferts are expected to remain challenging, making stacking searches informed by X-ray observations the most promising approach for discovering them within the next decade. Our results demonstrate that joint analyses across multiple neutrino telescopes, together with future MeV gamma-ray observations, will be essential for establishing Seyfert galaxies as astrophysical neutrino sources and provide a means for testing the coronal origin of their neutrino emission.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13255.title: Understanding Coronal `Seeing' using High Angular Resolution Radio Observations of Active Solar Emissions
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13255.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13255v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Solar radio bursts are generated through the plasma emission mechanism by beams of accelerated electrons travelling along magnetic field lines. They serve as powerful probes of the ambient coronal plasma and magnetic fields. At low frequencies, however, propagation through the turbulent, magnetised coronal plasma strongly modifies their observed properties. Disentangling these propagation effects from the intrinsic nature of the emission therefore remains a major challenge. Despite the long history of observations, there are only a few that leverage high-angular-resolution imaging. This is primarily due to the prevailing expectations that scattering from coronal density inhomogeneities significantly increases the apparent source size, obscuring any fine-scale structures that might be present. While small-scale features are routinely observed in EUV and X-rays, few are detected at meter wavelengths. Numerous studies have focused on quantifying the effect of scattering on the observed apparent size of a point solar radio source. Naturally, their results vary significantly depending on the specifics of the model used to describe coronal inhomogeneities and the scattering prescription applied -- ranging from sub-arcseconds to arcminutes. Recent high angular resolution observations with the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) -pathfinders, uGMRT and LOFAR, have revealed unexpectedly compact sources, with sizes as small as $\sim9$ arcseconds in type-I noise storms. Forthcoming high-fidelity and angular resolution SKAO observations will transform our understanding of solar radio emissions by constraining scattering models, improving coronal diagnostics, and revealing fine structures crucial for understanding solar radio emissions and propagation effects.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13257.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13257.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13257v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Exoplanet imaging is the main method for detailed characterization of planets orbiting beyond 1 au but it requires suppressing the bright glare of the star to see the faint planet light. As well as sophisticated instrumentation, effective image processing is necessary for starlight suppression, which continues to be a substantial limitation. Standard algorithms use reference images for starlight modelling and thus they are limited by inevitable telescope instabilities that change from reference to science observation. Addressing this challenge will increase the number of planets amenable to direct imaging and will be a notable step towards imaging exo-Earths with future observatories. Here we present a new physics-based method for starlight subtraction. Our method combines a multistep optimization with a flexible physical model to produce a starlight model, allowing modelling and compensation of instrument instabilities. We use automatic differentiation (autodiff) to optimize millions of model parameters. We demonstrate our method on observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Near-InfraRed Camera (NIRCam) coronagraph instrument. We achieve sensitivity 2-15 times superior to standard techniques, including the first detection of 51 Eridani b at 4.3 $\mu$m. This is the first time, to our knowledge, that such an approach has demonstrated substantially improved sensitivity on real, on-sky coronagraphic imaging. Our framework can be extended to other current and future ground-based and space-based observatories, including the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), potentially relaxing the unprecedented stability requirements needed to make these a success.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13260.title: Beyond the Fast Rotators: A JWST Multi-Cycle Treasury Survey of Substellar Weather
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13260.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13260v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Atmospheric variability provides a unique window into the three-dimensional structure, dynamics, and evolution of brown dwarf and giant exoplanet atmospheres. Recent JWST time-resolved spectroscopic observations have revealed complex wavelength-dependent variability, offering unprecedented insights into cloud structures, thermal perturbations, and atmospheric chemistry. However, existing programs have focused primarily on individual benchmarks and specific scientific questions, resulting in heterogeneous spectral and temporal coverage and leaving important regions of the substellar population underexplored, particularly across a broad range of rotation periods, spectral types, and viewing geometries. A JWST Multi-Cycle Treasury program could systematically investigate substellar weather across a diverse, well-characterized population. By combining broad infrared spectroscopic coverage with observations spanning multiple rotations and strategically selected epochs, this program would constrain the contributions of different physical mechanisms while investigating how atmospheric structures depend on rotation, viewing geometry, and fundamental physical properties. Extended monitoring would also improve rotational-period determinations and reveal how atmospheric features evolve from rotation to rotation and over longer timescales. This coordinated effort would provide a consistently designed and uniformly processed dataset of time-resolved spectra and variability diagnostics, enabling population-level comparisons, testing predictions from three-dimensional circulation models, and establishing a framework for interpreting the atmospheric diversity and evolution of brown dwarfs and directly imaged giant exoplanets.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13299.title: Cryohydrologic Flow and Pingo Formation Within Freezing Impact Melts in Occator Crater, Ceres
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13299.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13299v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ceres is a volatile-rich dwarf planet in the asteroid belt and a potential relict ocean world. It exhibits surface features indicative of subsurface brine activity, particularly within Occator Crater. High-resolution imagery from NASA's Dawn Mission reveals landslides, gullies, carbonate faculae, and mound-like features resembling terrestrial pingos on the floor of Occator Crater. Some of these landforms have been hypothesized to form from water, either from the ascent of deep crustal brines or from the freezeout of impact melt. Here, we test the hypothesis that pingo-like features can be formed via the freezing of shallow impact melts. We simulate the heat transfer and groundwater flow dynamics of a freezing impact melt deposit on the floor of Occator Crater. We test a comprehensive parameter space of regolith physical and material properties relevant to the cerean environment. We find that impact melt freezinf produces pressure gradients sufficient to drive hydrologic flow within the melt matrix and could transport fluids to the near surface through hydraulic fracturing. For most of the parameter space tested, water volumes delivered to pingo candidates on the surface meet or exceed those likely required for pingo formation. Analogous hydrologic processes may be important in the shallow subsurface of other regions of Occator Crater and Ceres at large as well as other ice-rich planetary bodies.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13321.title: The climate and potential habitability of a warm and oxygenated Mars
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13321.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13321v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present the first 3-D Global Climate Model simulations of an oxygen-rich, terraformed Mars. Assuming an O2-CO2 atmosphere, with additional warming from a well-mixed grey gas, we study (1) how surface temperatures change with atmospheric pressure and grey gas opacity, and (2) how temperature, pressure, and other effects limit life as oxygen builds up. We neglect the climate effects of dust and the water cycle, as well as possible soil-chemistry and nutrient limits to life. We find that (1) increasing grey gas opacity and increasing atmospheric pressure both moderate day-night temperature swings, but only slightly reduce seasonal temperature swings. Climate remains harsher in the Southern mid-latitudes relative to the Northern hemisphere. (2) For an atmospheric pressure of 30 hPa (5 times its present-day value), temperatures on Mars would be consistent with lichen and moss, followed at 60 hPa by forests (initially in the Hellas Basin). However, creating a human-breathable atmosphere through photosynthesis alone, at the oxygen production rates of biomes on Earth today, would take at least thousands of years, and require more oxygen than can be made via photosynthesis of known CO2 reserves on Mars alone (unless CO2 is recycled).

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13343.title: A TESS Disappearing Act: The Vanishing Transits of TOI-2535 b
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13343.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13343v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Planetary transits require a fortuitous alignment between a planet's orbit and our line of sight, but dynamical interactions can render this geometric coincidence only temporary. We report the discovery of the hot Jupiter TOI-2535 b, the first confirmed planet orbiting a single star whose transits have been directly observed to disappear. Over seven years of photometry from NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), the planet's transit chord traversed and eventually moved off the stellar disk entirely, with an impact parameter changing at the rate of $\dot{b} = 0.16\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. The transit mid-times also show significant departures of $\pm 6$ hours from a linear ephemeris. Joint modeling of the transit timing and duration variations (TTVs and TDVs) and NEID radial-velocity data indicates the presence of a nearby, mutually inclined ($i_\mathrm{mut} \gtrsim 5^\circ$) planetary perturber, with the TDV being primarily due to precession of the planets' orbital planes. Our dynamical modeling reveals that the perturber is likely of Saturn-mass or greater and in a mean-motion resonance with TOI-2535 b, making this an unusual system that contains two short-period giant planets. The TDVs measured for TOI-2535 b represent one of the most extreme examples of planet-planet interactions driving orbital evolution on human timescales.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13345.title: Millimeter-Wavelength Constraints on Circular Polarization of the Cosmic Microwave Background at Arcminute Scales with the Simons Array
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13345.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13345v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present constraints on the cosmic microwave background (CMB) circular polarization anisotropy at arcminute angular scales, using dedicated measurements from the Simons Array taken with a quarter-wave plate and rotating half-wave plate. A detection of circular polarization in the CMB would probe a range of proposed generation mechanisms, from Standard Model astrophysics to physics beyond it. At an observing frequency of 90 GHz, we place constraints over the multipole range $300 \leq \ell \leq 2000$, corresponding to angular scales of 5.4-36 arcmin, in bands of width $\Delta \ell = 100$, roughly tripling the highest multipole previously reached by a $V$-mode power spectrum measurement. Within this domain, we constrain the 95% confidence upper bound of $\ell (\ell+1) C_\ell^{VV} / (2\pi)$ to range from ${\sim}22\,\mu\mathrm{K}_\mathrm{CMB}^2$ at the $\ell = 350$ bandpower to ${\sim}3.5\times10^3\,\mu\mathrm{K}_\mathrm{CMB}^2$ at the $\ell = 1950$ bandpower. These limits are derived from ${\sim}2.5$ months of observations of each of two small regions of the sky located away from the Galactic plane, totaling ${\sim}12\,\mathrm{deg}^2$ of effective sky area. Because the methodology of this study marginalizes known foreground contamination, these bounds serve as robust, conservative limits on the true CMB circular polarization signal down to the sensitivity limits of the instrument. Additionally, we provide an experimental and analytical framework for implementing circular polarization observations on other telescopes by utilizing a quarter-wave plate and half-wave plate design.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13350.title: Early--Narrow and Late--Wide Populations of GRB X-ray Flares
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13350.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13350v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The physical origin of gamma-ray burst (GRB) X-ray flares remains debated, particularly whether they arise from prolonged central-engine activity or from variability in the external shock. Building on our previous analysis of 89 Swift GRBs with measured redshifts, we investigate the rest-frame temporal properties of X-ray flares detected in 61 bursts. We apply a multivariate Gaussian Mixture Model to rest-frame peak times and widths. We identify two statistically distinct populations: early-narrow flares (80%), with characteristic peak times of approximately 10^2 s and w/t_pk <= 1, and late-wide flares (20%), with characteristic peak times of ~ 10^3.5 s and w/t_pk >= 2. Of the 61 single or first flares, 55 belong to the early-narrow population and only 6 to the late-wide population. Of the 36 second flares, 23 (64%) belong to the early-narrow population, with shorter waiting times, whereas 13 (36%) belong to the late-wide population, with substantially longer waiting times. The width-peak-time correlation remains significant for early-narrow flares but not for late-wide flares. Furthermore, we find no correlation between flare width and energy. We find a decline of flare luminosity with peak time, driven primarily by the early-narrow population, but not statistically significant for late-wide flares. These results imply that a simple shift in time, potentially associated with later episodes of central-engine activity, cannot explain the distinction between the two flare populations. On the other hand, the peak times are consistent with expectations from an accretion disk formed following the collapse of a stellar-size massive star. Combined with our previous finding that flare properties are independent of the presence of an X-ray plateau, these results favor prolonged accretion-driven central-engine activity over external-shock variability as the primary origin of X-ray flares.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13364.title: Identification of the C IV $\lambda\lambda$5801, 5812 Emission in the Off-Nuclear TDE 2025abcr
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13364.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13364v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: TDE 2025abcr is a tidal disruption event (TDE) located approximately 9 kpc in projection from its host galaxy nucleus. Our spectroscopic follow-up with the Very Large Telescope (VLT) reveals C IV $\lambda\lambda5801, 5812$ emission, representing the first identification of this C IV doublet in a TDE. These transitions are uncommon in active galactic nuclei (AGN) spectra but have been observed in supernova flash spectra and Wolf-Rayet (WR) stars. We propose that the doublet arises from the combined effects of continuum fluorescence and photon trapping in the 312 \r{A} transition, analogous to the mechanism operating in nitrogen-sequence Wolf-Rayet (WN) winds. This mechanism requires intense extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) illumination and a high optical depth, providing a distinctive diagnostic of the physical conditions in optically thick TDE outflows. These requirements, together with the relatively narrow widths of the broad emission lines, the presence of Bowen fluorescence features, and the small inferred blackbody radius, favor a compact and dense envelope in TDE 2025abcr. The optical C IV doublet may have been overlooked in previous observational and theoretical studies of TDEs, motivating more detailed radiative-transfer calculations for optically thick outflows. With future TDE samples from Rubin/LSST and WFST, a larger C IV TDE sample will test if this population systematically favors a compact photosphere.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13391.title: Flux Variation of the Crab Pulsar Observed Using Fermi LAT and NuSTAR
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13391.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13391v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The flux of pulsed emission from the Crab pulsar, just like most of other pulsars, is considered to be steady over time scales much larger than the pulsation period, except for a smooth, secular decrease related to the aging of pulsars. Such a steady assumption prevails in all theoretical investigations of pulsar emission models. However, here we report the discovery of stochastic fluctuation in the flux and photon index of the Crab pulsar gamma-ray and X-ray emissions utilizing archival data of Fermi LAT (0.1 -- 100 GeV, spanning 17 years) and of NuSTAR (3.0 -- 79.0 keV, spanning 13 years) observations. The origin of such fluctuation is intriguing. It might be related to possible configuration adjustment of magnetic fields in neutron stars' superconducting and superfluid interiors.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13502.title: Thermal-pulse-resolved Binary Population Synthesis with Detailed Stellar Models: Implications for Long-period WD+MS Formation
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13502.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13502v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The origin of the long-orbital-period white dwarf--main-sequence (WD+MS) binaries revealed by Gaia challenges the traditional association of common-envelope evolution (CEE) with short orbital periods. We develop a thermal-pulse-resolved binary population synthesis framework based on 51 detailed MESA evolutionary tracks with initial masses of 1--6 $M_{\odot}$. Applying these tracks to $5\times10^6$ initially sampled binaries, we follow the time-dependent stellar radius, wind mass loss, angular momentum, and tidal interactions, while calculating the envelope binding energy directly from the donor structure at the onset of Roche-lobe overflow. We find that thermal pulses can trigger binary interaction through envelope expansion and tidal orbital shrinkage, while the weakly bound envelopes of highly evolved thermally pulsing asymptotic giant branch (TP-AGB) donors allow CE ejection with limited orbital contraction. For our standard model, with $\alpha_{\mathrm{CE}}$ = 0.3 and $\alpha_{\mathrm{th}}$ = 0.5, systems with orbital periods above 30 days constitute approximately 11.5\% of the resulting TP-AGB-initiated post-CE binaries (PCEBs). Long-period PCEBs can form across a large range of CE parameters and can reach periods of several hundred days even without any internal-energy contribution when $\alpha_{\mathrm{CE}}$ = 1. Their WD masses peak near 0.6 $M_\odot$, whereas systems containing more massive WDs are rare. Moreover, long-period PCEBs closely follow the single-star initial--final mass relation, providing a potential diagnostic of their formation channel in clusters, where progenitor masses can be independently constrained. Our results identify late TP-AGB CEE as a viable contributor to the observed long-period WD+MS population.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13505.title: A Possible Non-Transiting Companion in the TOI-2109 System Supported by Transit Timing Variations
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13505.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13505v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Transit timing variations are a powerful method for detecting non-transiting planets, particularly in systems near mean-motion resonances. We investigate the ultra-short-period hot Jupiter TOI-2109 b using 87 transit epochs spanning two decades (2006-2025), combining observations from TESS, CHEOPS, HST, and ground-based photometry. We compare five timing models representing different physical scenarios: a linear ephemeris, orbital decay, apsidal precession, a sinusoidal model, and a two-planet n-body dynamical model. The orbital-decay fit yields $\dot{P} = -3.96 \pm 2.05$ ms yr$^{-1}$, providing no significant evidence for ongoing orbital decay. The sinusoidal model reveals a periodic transit-timing-variation signal with an amplitude of $\approx 44\,s$. Dynamical modelling favours an additional non-transiting companion near the 7:3 mean-motion resonance with an orbital period of $1.57813\pm 8.9\times10^{-5}$ days and a mass of $0.70 \pm 0.02\,M_{\rm Jup}$. The two-planet model yields $\Delta \mathrm{BIC}=4.95$ relative to the sinusoidal model, indicating positive evidence that the observed transit timing variations are best explained by gravitational perturbations from an additional planet.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13506.title: AGN feedback destroying group cool cores --- a case study on IC 2476 with a remnant radio AGN and an exceptionally low abundance
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13506.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13506v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present results from deep XMM-Newton observations ($\sim$180 ksec) of the galaxy group IC 2476 in the X-GAP sample, capturing a rare AGN feedback regime, where the central radio AGN has ceased activity but the radio lobes are still detectable. The hot intragroup medium of IC 2476 features a compact cool core, with a size of ~10 kpc, and a moderate X-ray luminosity of $\sim3.4\times10^{40}$ erg/s. We measured an unusually low temperature of $\sim$0.45 keV within the cool core. We measured an exceptionally low abundance of below ~0.2 solar, even in the central region. The X-ray surface brightness of the group is not symmetric and shows a clear depression in the region overlaid with the eastern radio lobe, suggesting the presence of an X-ray cavity. The scaled entropy of the hot gas within 0.1 r500 of IC 2476 is among the highest in X-ray galaxy groups with a similar system temperature. Our study suggests that the past powerful radio AGN outburst in IC 2476 has disrupted the cool core and the X-ray cavity has dissipated or mixed with the surrounding hot gas since the shutdown of the central AGN. A large cool core may be gradually re-established in the absence of AGN activity. This system therefore provides a great example of AGN feedback destroying the group cool core, even with a moderate radio luminosity at present.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13518.title: The UV luminosity function at 1.6 < z < 2.2 from UVCANDELS
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13518.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13518v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present an analysis of the rest-frame UV luminosity function (LF) of galaxies at $1.6<2.2$ using the UVCANDELS F435W imaging data. Restricting our analysis to sources above $30\%$ completeness to minimize uncertainties at the faint end, we construct a catalog of 5,212 galaxies at $1.6<2.2$ down to an absolute magnitude of $M_{\rm UV} = -16.8$, using well-tested photometric redshifts. We perform a maximum likelihood estimate to derive the best-fit Schechter parameters of the UV LF at a median redshift of $z\sim1.9$. We report a best-fit faint-end slope of $\alpha = -1.586 \pm 0.042$. Splitting the sample into two redshift bins, we obtain $\alpha=-1.488 \pm 0.055$ at $z\sim1.75$ and $\alpha=-1.604 \pm 0.066$ at $z\sim2.05$ ($\sim1.4\sigma$ difference), alongside a $\sim2.3\sigma$ brightening in $M^{*}$. Integrating our best-fit LF down to $M_{\rm UV} = -15$, we derive $\rho_{\rm UV} = (1.821 \pm 0.037) \times 10^{26}\ \rm erg\ s^{-1}\ Hz^{-1}\ Mpc^{-3}$ at $z\sim1.9$. Combining our F435W measurements with previous UVCANDELS F275W results and other literature data, we model the redshift evolution of $\rho_{\rm UV}$ from $z\sim0$ to $z\sim10$.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13519.title: Molecular signatures of shocked gas and enhanced cosmic-ray ionization in supernova remnant W49B revealed by ALMA
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13519.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13519v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Galactic supernova remnants (SNRs) interacting with molecular clouds (MCs) provide important laboratories for investigating how supernova feedback is transferred to the interstellar medium. We performed observations of the HCO+ J=1-0, 3-2, and 4-3 lines, as well as the CO J=3-2 line, toward the eastern and western regions of SNR W49B using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) and the Atacama Pathfinder Experiment (APEX) telescope. In W49B west, we identify twelve regions with broad-line profiles in both HCO+ and CO emission, with FWHM of 25-60 km/s, providing clear evidence of SNR-MC interaction. These emissions are compact (at $\sim$5 arcsec resolution) and spatially coincident with 2.12~$\mu$m H$_2$ emission, but generally offset from the 1.64~$\mu$m [Fe~II] and radio continuum peaks. Non-LTE analyses yield shocked-gas densities of (0.5-1.6) $\times 10^5$~cm$^{-3}$ and high $N_{\rm HCO+}/N_{\rm CO}$ abundance ratios of (4.2-14.5) $\times 10^{-4}$. Reproducing such high abundance ratios in shocked MCs requires high cosmic ray ionization rates (CRIRs) of a few 10$^{-14}$-10$^{-13}$~s$^{-1}$, about 3-4 orders of magnitude above the standard Galactic level. Some regions exhibit enhanced HCO+/CO intensity ratios in their high-velocity line wings, possibly due to multiple unresolved shocks spanning a range of velocities and gas densities, spatial variations in the CRIR, or both. By contrast, the ratio remains nearly constant with velocity in other regions. For these regions, we further explore the propagation of low-energy CRs through the post-shock layer. An energy-budget analysis of a representative shocked clump indicates that the shock-associated kinetic-energy reservoir substantially exceeds cumulative CR and X-ray heating inputs, with CR heating exceeding X-ray heating.[abridged]

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13542.title: OASIS: A Fast Dynamical Halo Finding Algorithm
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13542.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13542v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In recent work (Garc\'ia et al. 2023), we advocated for defining a dynamical halo as the collection of particles that orbit their self-generated potential. Here we introduce the Orbiting-mass ASsIgnment Scheme (OASIS), a fast energy-based algorithm for constructing dynamical halo catalogs. Using single-snapshot information, OASIS achieves $\simeq 9\%$ scatter in orbiting mass estimates relative to the SPARTA particle-tracking algorithm. As an illustration of the applications enabled by OASIS, we use the Quijote and Erebos simulation suites to show that the $z=0$ dynamical halo mass function is nearly universal with respect to cosmology, and that it is well described by a modified Press-Schechter form with an effective collapse threshold $\delta_{\rm sc} = 1.54$ at intermediate masses. However, this description fails at high masses.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13567.title: The unified bound dark energy--bound dark matter model confronted with DESI DR2, ACT and SPT-3G, and the Unite supernovae measurements
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13567.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13567v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The unified bound dark energy-bound dark matter (BDE-BDM) model derives the whole dark sector from a single supersymmetric SU(3) dark gauge group, whose lightest meson is the dark energy and whose heavier bound states, created with a velocity $v_c$ when the group condenses, are the dark matter. Because the condensation scale $\Lambda_c$ is fixed by gauge-coupling unification, the dark-energy sector has no free parameter beyond those of $\Lambda$CDM, and the dark-matter sector adds only $v_c$. We confront the model with DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO), the Planck, ACT DR6 and SPT-3G D1 CMB spectra, the combined ACT and SPT CMB lensing and the Unite supernovae. The measured condensation scale, $\Lambda_c=43.74\pm0.11$ eV, lies inside the window $34^{+16}_{-11}$ eV predicted by unification, and the dark energy thaws without ever crossing the phantom divide, reaching $w_0=-0.9267\pm0.0003$ today; it thus reproduces the DESI distances that $w_0w_a$CDM fits with a phantom past. BDE-BDM gives the best fit to the DESI DR2 BAO of the four models, reducing $\chi^2_{\rm BAO}$ by 20% with respect to $\Lambda$CDM, more than $w_0w_a$CDM, and over the full data combination it is statistically equivalent to both $\Lambda$CDM and $w_0w_a$CDM, with $\ln B=-0.50$ and $-0.15$, while having two fewer dark-energy parameters than $w_0w_a$CDM. Within bound dark energy, bound dark matter is moderately preferred over cold dark matter, $\ln B=+3.2$ with $\Delta\chi^2=-9.0$, mostly from the CMB. The data now constrain the bound velocity from both sides, $v_c=0.37\pm0.14$, which places the free-streaming cutoff of the matter power spectrum at $k_{1/2}=1.49\,h$ Mpc$^{-1}$ and lowers the amplitude of structure to $S_8=0.807\pm0.007$. Future high-redshift and Lyman-$\alpha$ forest data, together with growth and lensing measurements, will therefore provide the decisive tests of the unified dark sector.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13717.title: Asteroseismology of the Gaia SB2 HD 70510: From Radial Modes to Component Masses
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13717.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13717v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Double-lined spectroscopic binary (SB2) orbits give mass ratios and projected component masses, but the absolute masses depend on the unknown inclination. HD 70510 is a Gaia DR3 SB2 in which regular $\delta$ Scuti pulsations constrain the properties of one component. We analyze nine sectors of TESS photometry and combine stellar evolution and pulsation modelling with a two-star spectral energy distribution (SED) fit to the unresolved Gaia and 2MASS photometry. Five high-signal-to-noise peaks form a sequence consistent with the radial fundamental mode and four consecutive overtones. Two stable pulsation clocks show the sign and amplitude expected from the orbital motion of the Gaia primary, identifying it as the pulsator. Combining the radial-mode and binary-SED fits with the Gaia SB2 orbit gives $M_1=1.594^{+0.026}_{-0.026}\,M_\odot$, $R_1=1.482^{+0.014}_{-0.012}\,R_\odot$, and an age of $171^{+112}_{-99}$ Myr. We obtain an orbital inclination of $i=82.1^{+3.5}_{-3.4}$ deg and a companion mass of $M_2=1.121^{+0.029}_{-0.028}\,M_\odot$. These intervals are statistical and remain conditional on the adopted radial-mode identification and stellar and binary-SED models. The primary lies close to the zero-age main sequence, while the roughly 6000-K companion contributes 14-28% of the unresolved optical-to-near-infrared flux. HD 70510 shows how regular pulsations can provide component masses for non-eclipsing TESS binaries with Gaia DR3 SB2 orbital solutions.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13729.title: Angular momentum transport in a newborn protostar--disc system: magnetic braking, spiral arms and the magneto-rotational instability
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13729.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13729v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Angular momentum transport in young protostar--disc systems involves magnetic braking, magneto-rotational turbulence and gravitational instability, mechanisms that are usually studied separately and on different scales. We present a three-dimensional non-ideal magnetohydrodynamic simulation, including Ohmic and ambipolar diffusion, that follows the collapse of a $1~M_\odot$ dense core continuously from the cloud scale to the formation of the protostar, and then the resulting protostar--disc system for $\sim 64~\mathrm{yr}$ at a resolution of $\sim 10^{-4}~\mathrm{AU}$ at the protostellar surface. We decompose the azimuthally averaged angular momentum budget into Reynolds, Maxwell and gravitational torques, each split into a radial and a meridional component, over a quasi-steady phase of the evolution. The collapse produces a thick disc an order of magnitude more massive than the protostar, whose specific angular momentum decreases as it accretes. Accretion through the disc is vertically layered, with accreting and decreting layers at the same radius, a pattern set layer by layer by the torques. The transport separates into three regimes delimited by the coupling of the magnetic field to the gas. Magnetic braking operates in the envelope. Maxwell stresses dominate inside $\sim 0.1~\mathrm{AU}$, where the field recouples and the magneto-rotational instability develops. In the ambipolar dead zone that makes up the bulk of the disc, the Reynolds stress dominates, carried by $m=2$ spiral arms in a marginally unstable disc, with the gravitational stress as a secondary contributor. Meridional transport is as important as radial transport, so that a one-dimensional viscous model fitted to the net mass flux would require a negative $\alpha$ over part of the disc.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13733.title: Scalar-Induced Gravitational Waves Probing Phase Transitions in the Standard Model and Beyond
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13733.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13733v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are unique messengers of physics in the early Universe and possible sources for the observed data from pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). It has been demonstrated that SIGWs have the potential to probe cosmological phase transitions via measurement of the equation of state and sound speed of the cosmic thermal bath, which have non-trivial time dependence during phase transitions. In this work, we improve on existing studies of SIGWs in a time-dependent background with time-dependent initial conditions and an entropy-conserving thermal history of the Standard Model (SM). We provide possible physical explanations for features of the gravitational wave spectrum from phase transitions, the most prominent of which for a scale-invariant curvature spectrum is a step due to entropy dilution. We show that current and future gravitational wave observations across a wide range of frequencies can probe phase transitions in the SM and physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM). Signals from the QCD crossover appear around 10 nHz, inside the observable window of PTAs. We perform data analyses using NANOGrav 15-year data, showing a mild preference for the QCD crossover over standard radiation domination for two choices of curvature spectra. BSM phase transitions in the TeV range lead to signals around mHz, which are accessible in future space-based experiments such as LISA, Taiji and TianQin.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13756.title: Self-Interacting Neutrinos in NEDE and DRMD Cosmologies: Posteriors, profiles and evidence using CLiENT
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13756.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13756v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A large number of extensions of the $\Lambda$CDM model have been proposed as solutions to the Hubble tension, but they are almost always tested separately. Combinations of such models are rarely studied, and one reason is that their parameter spaces are very costly to explore with standard methods. Here we study a combination of two models which have each been proposed as a solution: self-interacting neutrinos (SI$
u$) and the dark radiation matter decoupling (DRMD) of hot new early dark energy. The SI$
u$+DRMD model has twelve cosmological parameters, a bimodal posterior in the neutrino self-interaction and several flat directions in parameter space, and it can only be investigated in detail because we use the likelihood emulator CLiENT. With emulators trained on about $3	imes 10^5$ likelihood evaluations per dataset we obtain posteriors, best fits and profile likelihoods for the model and for the models nested within it, and all quoted $\chi^2$ values are calculated with the true likelihood. We use two data combinations, both with and without the SH0ES calibration: a conservative one consisting of Planck, DESI BAO and Pantheon+ supernovae, and a more aggressive one in which the small-scale CMB spectra come from ACT and SPT. With the most aggressive combination, the SI$
u$+DRMD model provides a much better fit than either SI$
u$ or DRMD on its own, and its posterior gives $H_0 = 70.94\pm 0.60$ km/s/Mpc. It lowers the $\chi^2$ of $\Lambda$CDM by 27.6, compared with 9.9 for DRMD and 4.0 for SI$
u$, i.e. by more than the sum of the two ($\Delta$AIC = -15.7 relative to DRMD, in terms of the Akaike information criterion). This shows that combined models can fit the data considerably better than the individual models, and it demonstrates the value of being able to analyse such complex models in detail.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13770.title: ExoPlanetLab: Bayesian orbit fitting of Gaia-DR4 epoch astrometry, radial velocities and relative astrometry
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13770.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13770v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gaia Data Release 4 (DR4) provides epoch astrometry from which thousands of giant planets and many substellar and stellar companions can be characterised. We present ExoPlanetLab, an open-source package for Bayesian orbit inference from Gaia epoch astrometry, radial velocities (RVs) and relative astrometry, validated on simulated and real data. The model orbit is compared with the epoch residuals after removing the part absorbed by the single-star fit. A Student-t likelihood describes heavy-tailed data. A robust Keplerian periodogram with bootstrap false-alarm probabilities gives starting values for a joint fit. Five samplers are available: tempered ensemble MCMC, two nested samplers and two reversible-jump samplers. Evidences for a fixed number of companions select that number. Acceleration and scan-angle models test whether an orbit is warranted. The samplers agree within 0.1 sigma on a simulated two-planet system. In 180 injections all fits converge, and all signals with signal-to-noise ratio S >= 10 are detected. The posteriors show no significant bias, but the period coverage is below nominal: 90% of the true periods lie within their 95% credible intervals. None of 30 companion-free data sets gives a false detection. On DR4 pre-release data the orbit of Gaia BH3 is recovered within 1.4 sigma of published solutions. The Student-t model brings the astrometric period and eccentricity of HD 114762 onto its RV orbit. Eight simulated relative positions narrow the period's credible interval to 0.27 of its width, and Octofitter agrees within 0.2 sigma on the same data. The code is validated for single sources with DR4-like epoch astrometry, with or without RVs. Relative astrometry is tested on simulated data only. The main limits are an uncorrelated noise model and the computing cost, which grows linearly with the number of measurements and steeply with the number of companions.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13771.title: Breaking the Chain: The Dynamical History of the Barnard's Star Planetary System
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13771.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13771v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Barnard's Star is the nearest single-star system to the Sun and hosts four recently detected sub-Earth-mass planets. The system exhibits architectural imprints of a "broken resonant chain". We explore scenarios in which the presence of a now-lost, additional planet provides a more natural explanation for the present-day architecture from a dynamical-formation perspective. In such a situation, a resonance-breaking event triggered a merger between two planets, forming the present-day planet c. We find two viable pathways that can reproduce the observed configuration: (i) stellar-driven, long-term tidal expansion and (ii) disk-driven, early expansion, in which one-sided Lindblad torques separate the two outermost planets. Both scenarios can lead to the c1-c2 merger required to form the present-day architecture. The latter pathway also agrees with the broader exoplanet census: among the 14 compact four-planet systems we identify with broken-chain architectures similar to Barnard's Star system, ten have the third planet "breaking" the resonant sequence.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13806.title: Impact of Primordial Magnetic Field-induced Small-scale Power on Non-linear Structure Formation and Cosmic Reionization
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13806.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13806v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) can enhance small-scale matter perturbations and alter halo formation and reionization. We evolve PMF-modified initial spectra with collisionless $N$-body simulations and use the halo catalogues as sources for semi-numerical ionization and 21-cm brightness-temperature fields in the saturated spin-temperature limit. We compare $\Lambda$CDM with four PMF models, $B_0=100$, $130$, $150$, and $170\,\mathrm{pG}$, at $n_B=-2.9$. With cosmology and source prescriptions fixed, the PMF models show enhanced small-scale clustering, more early low-mass haloes and earlier reionization. Their volume-averaged reionization midpoints advance by $\Delta z_{50}\simeq0.50$--$2.14$, with changes in ionization morphology and 21-cm power spectra. The Thomson optical depth rises from $\tau_{\rm e}\simeq0.0547$ for $\Lambda$CDM to $0.0595$--$0.0786$. These simulation-relative offsets span $0.66$--$3.28$ times the Planck 2018 uncertainty, $\sigma_\tau=0.0073$, and are not exclusion significances. The common source efficiency $N_{\rm ion}$ is calibrated to a reference history approaching ionization completion near $z\sim6$ and an optical depth close to Planck 2018, without model-specific retuning. We omit subsequent magnetic-field evolution and dissipative magnetic heating. Observational bounds require joint treatment of astrophysical degeneracies and numerical uncertainties.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13825.title: On the Existence of an Equilibrium Density Profile for Massive Collisional Star Clusters
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13825.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13825v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The dynamical evolution of massive, dense star clusters is governed by a complex interplay of multiple physical processes, including two-body relaxation, strong encounters, stellar evolution, and galactic tides, superimposed on the orbital motion of individual stars and binaries within the cluster potential. These processes can alter the internal evolution of individual stars and binaries, produce exotic stellar objects, and collectively determine the global structural evolution of the cluster. In this paper, we use the Monte Carlo star cluster evolution code CMC-COSMIC to study how the density profiles of dense star clusters evolve under the combined effects of these processes. We find that for a given initial mass and binding energy, cluster models converge toward a characteristic density profile largely independent of their initial density distributions. This convergence occurs during the late-time, quasi-static phase of evolution, when gravitational contraction is balanced by energy generated through black hole binaries in the cluster core. The shape of this profile is well represented by a King profile with W_0=6.8 but with the virial radius of the final cluster larger than the initial by a factor of about 7. We further show that this equilibrium profile is dynamically stable, i.e., perturbations away from it decay through the cluster's natural dynamical evolution, driving the system back toward the equilibrium profile.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13829.title: Stable cosmology under flexible covariances: Rescaling and cross-survey correlations in DESI BAO and supernova data
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13829.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13829v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Combinations of cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO), and Type Ia supernova (SN) data currently favor evolving dark energy over $\Lambda$CDM at the $\sim 3$--$4\sigma$ level, making it important to test whether this preference could be driven by imperfectly modeled uncertainties. We introduce a phenomenological framework in which the published covariance of each dataset is rescaled by a free parameter and the SN compilations are allowed effective cross-survey correlations. We apply it to DESI DR2 BAO, Planck 2018 temperature and polarization data, and a joint likelihood of Pantheon+, Union3, and DES-Dovekie constructed on a common redshift basis. The DESI, Union3, and DES-Dovekie data are consistent with their published covariances, while Pantheon+ shows a mild preference for additional covariance. In all cases the data still allow error bars up to $\sim 1.7$ times larger than published at 95% credibility, yet freeing the rescaling parameters improves the best fit by $\Delta\chi^2 < 1$. Pantheon+ and Union3 exhibit a clear positive effective correlation, $r\simeq 0.4$--$0.5$, plausibly reflecting their shared supernovae; the Pantheon+--DES-Dovekie correlation is weaker and model dependent, and the Union3--DES-Dovekie correlation is consistent with zero. The added covariance freedom broadens the cosmological constraints without shifting them: for the full data combination, the improvement of $w_0w_a$CDM over $\Lambda$CDM changes only from $\Delta\chi^2 = 12.8$ to $12.3$ (nominally $3.15\sigma$ to $3.07\sigma$). The preference for evolving dark energy is therefore robust to covariance misestimation of the form considered here.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13833.title: Cross-experiment tests of the atmospheric-muon excess
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13833.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13833v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-energy cosmic rays produce atmospheric muons through cascades of hadronic interactions, yet simulations often underestimate the muon content of extensive air showers. Whether the same problem affects energetic atmospheric muons, which probe a different part of the cascade, is less clear. Here we compare published atmospheric-muon measurements from four experiments with reference predictions based on a shared choice of hadronic interaction model and primary cosmic-ray flux. We find that the measurements predominantly exceed the central predictions across different experimental techniques, from surface measurements to deep detectors. This recurring excess is more consistent across the measurements than any inferred dependence on energy or zenith angle. These atmospheric muons preferentially originate from energetic mesons produced early in the cascade, whereas the total muon content of extensive air showers also reflects interactions at later stages. A common explanation of both excesses must therefore increase the effective supply of energetic muon parents, rather than merely increasing the multiplicity of soft particles. This provides a way to distinguish between competing explanations of the cosmic-ray muon puzzle.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13835.title: Tracing early galaxies back in time: implications for the dearth of galaxies beyond z~15
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13835.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13835v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Although the James Webb Space Telescope has pushed the observational frontier to $z\sim14$, the onset of star formation in the earliest galaxies remains beyond direct reach, making the star formation histories (SFH) of observed galaxies a key tool for probing earlier epochs. We develop and validate a new SFH model based on an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, capable of reproducing the bursty star formation expected in high-redshift galaxies. Tested on the SPHINX$^{20}$ mock catalogs, it accurately recovers stellar masses and SFRs and reconstructs cumulative SFHs at population level; the formation redshift is well constrained at $z\gtrsim9$ but not at $z\sim8$. Applied to 400 galaxies at $9<15$ from the UNICORN/GOODS-South sample, we find that sources observed at $z<10$ typically reached 20% of their stellar mass no earlier than $z\sim12$, disfavoring a clear evolutionary link to spectroscopically confirmed galaxies at $z\gtrsim13$. Among 218 galaxies at $10<15$, only 28 had formed 20% of their stellar mass by $z=15$, with a median formation redshift $z_{\rm form,20\%}=16.9^{+1.1}_{-1.1}$, and 24% of our sample had already reached $10^7$M$_{\odot}$ by $z=15$. At $z=17$, only 11 of these 28 galaxies had reached 20% of their stellar mass. The derived survey areas required to detect them are consistent with or slightly more optimistic than previous constraints at the bright end, and larger than some literature estimates at the faint end. At $z=20$, a single galaxy had formed 20% of its stellar mass, yielding a tentative constraint of one object at $M_{\rm UV}=-18.1\pm0.6$ per $\sim200$\,arcmin$^2$. Our results suggest a relatively slow decline in star formation activity between $z\sim15$ and $z\sim17$, followed by a more rapid decline up to $z\sim20$.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13836.title: Deriving physical parameters of unresolved star clusters. X. Size evolution of young star clusters in the M31 disc
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13836.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13836v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Context. Star cluster structural properties and their correlations with other cluster parameters (age, mass, galactocentric distance) provide key constraints on cluster formation and dynamical evolution within star-forming galactic discs. In the tenth paper of this series, we analysed structural parameters of 1918 young star clusters (up to 800 Myr) in the disc of M31. Aims. We aim to examine the structural evolution of M31 disc clusters and determine how their sizes correlate with physical and spatial properties. Our goal is to improve the understanding of cluster formation and evolution in spiral galaxy discs. Methods. We use the M31 disc cluster parameter catalogue based on photometric measurements of the Panchromatic Hubble Andromeda Treasury survey data. We perform statistical analysis to determine how cluster structural parameters relate to their physical characteristics and location within the disc. Results. Young clusters in the disc of M31 are compact ($R_{50}\sim1.8$ pc) and expand rapidly during the first $\sim$20 Myr, more than doubling in size. At older ages, M31 clusters follow a weak age-radius relation $(R_{50}\propto t^{0.12\pm0.01}\,\,)$. We find no significant correlation between cluster size and galactocentric distance, indicating that internal processes dominate their early evolution, with minimal impact from the galactic tidal field. Our results suggest that stellar-evolution-driven mass loss and internal dynamical interactions are likely drivers of early cluster structural evolution in the M31 disc. A shallow mass-radius relation emerges for clusters older than 100 Myr $(R_{50}\propto M^{0.18\pm0.01}\,\,)$, while the trend for younger clusters remains uncertain. The diversity of mass-radius relations observed in nearby spiral galaxies, both within and beyond the Local Group, highlights the need for further theoretical work on cluster formation and evolution.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13837.title: Measuring the Milky Way potential with the phase snail shape curves
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13837.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13837v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Aims. Phase spirals found in the vertical phase-space ($z-V_z$) indicate that the Galactic disk is in disequilibrium. Although the origin remains elusive, the wrapping of phase snails is dominated by the vertical potential profiles, naturally encoding potential information in their shapes.
  Methods. To measure the Galactic potential, we extracted the phase snail shape curves from density contrast maps and transformed them into the vertical frequency-action angle ($\Omega_z - \theta_z$) space via orbital integration, then performed linear fitting to derive potential parameters. We verified our method with a test particle simulation.
  Results. Our method performs well in the test particle simulation, with the recovered Galactic vertical potential profiles in excellent agreement with the input potential models. We also apply our method to the observed phase snails with guiding center radii in the range of $8\le R_g\le11$ kpc. Utilizing snail shape curves only, the model derived vertical potential profiles agree with popular Milky Way potential models. The model yields a Galactic virial mass of $M_{200}= 0.81^{+0.22}_{-0.23} \times10^{12}\, {\rm M_{\odot}}$ and a local dark matter density of $\rho_{dm,\odot}= 0.0076^{+0.0019}_{-0.0021} \,{\rm M_{\odot}\,pc^{-3}}$, consistent with the literature, but with a flatter rotation curve than the observation. To better constrain the Galactic potential, we further combine the phase snails and the rotation curve. The improved model results in $M_{200}= 0.87^{+0.31}_{-0.33} \times10^{12}\, {\rm M_{\odot}}$ and $\rho_{dm,\odot}= 0.0097^{+0.0002}_{-0.0009} \,{\rm M_{\odot}\,pc^{-3}}$. The high precision of $\rho_{dm,\odot}$ results from the joint constraints in the solar neighborhood. We also obtain an estimation of the perturbation time in a range of 400-750 Myr with a median of 564 Myr, consistent with recent measurements. (abridged)

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13844.title: Log-normal behavior of Optical Polarization in a sample of Blazars: Evidence for Multiplicative Magneto-hydrodynamic Processes in Relativistic Jets
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13844.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13844v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Optical synchrotron polarization is one of the most direct probes of the magnetic-field structure and particle-acceleration processes in the relativistic jets of blazars. Although long-term optical flux variability is often attributed to multiplicative stochastic processes because of its log-normal behavior, but the physical origin of optical polarization variability remains less understood. In this study, we investigate the long-term optical flux and polarization variability of a sample of blazars using nearly a decade of photo-polarimetric observations from the Steward Observatory. We find that, like the optical flux, the optical degree of polarization is generally well described by a log-normal distribution and shows an approximately linear relationship between its variability amplitude and mean value. We interpret this behavior within a magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) framework in which the magnetic-field undergoes repeated stochastic changes driven by shocks, turbulence, velocity shear, and large-scale jet dynamics. The cumulative effect of these processes can naturally generate multiplicative variability, leaving similar statistical signatures in both the synchrotron flux and the degree of polarization. Our results provide new observational evidence that the long-term statistical behavior of optical flux and polarization may arise from a common set of MHD processes associated with magnetic-field evolution.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13881.title: Dust in Stellar Populations: Grid-Based and Bayesian Spectral Energy Distribution Fitting of AGB Stars with SEDust and MCM-SEDust
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13881.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13881v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Dust shapes the spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of stellar populations on every scale, from the circumstellar envelopes of evolved stars to the interstellar medium of galaxies. We review the ingredients of stellar population synthesis (SPS) models: the initial mass function, stellar evolutionary tracks, stellar spectral libraries, and dust models. We then present SEDust, an automated pipeline that finds the best- fitting DUSTY radiative-transfer model for the SEDs of dusty asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars, and MCM-SEDust, its extension. We discuss how both connect the physics of individual dusty stars to the dust budget of stellar populations.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13951.title: A Virgo Environmental Survey Tracing Ionised Gas Emission (VESTIGE). XXIII. NGC 4569 past orbit reconstruction with ORFEO
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13951.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13951v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Extended ionised gas tails can preserve a dynamical record of a galaxy's recent interaction with the intracluster medium (ICM). Recovering that history from the observed tail requires solving an inverse dynamical problem tied to the physical conditions for gas removal. We present the first application of ORFEO to NGC 4569, using the sky positions and line-of-sight (LOS) velocities of the galaxy and 94 H$\alpha$-emitting regions to reconstruct its recent orbit and tail chronology. The model combines data with gas surface-density constraints, a spherical Virgo Cluster A gravitational potential derived with MG-MAMPOSSt, and an X-ray-based ICM density profile. For an assumed LOS distance, it infers its orbit and ram-pressure history. At the fiducial distance $d_0=16.5$ Mpc, ORFEO recovers a coherent phase-space sequence with a dynamical tail age $T_{\rm tail}=250^{+37}_{-19}$ Myr. The ram-pressure maximum occurred at $t_{P_{\rm ram},{\rm peak}}=-163^{+11}_{-15}$ Myr, close to the nearest approach to the Virgo Cluster A centre at $305^{+19}_{-25}$ kpc, placing NGC 4569 after peak ram pressure. Scanning the LOS distance does not select a unique solution but separates comparably fitting reconstructions into a low-distance post-peak branch and a high-distance pre-peak branch. Comparison with an independent stripping threshold at the observed disc truncation radius favours the low-distance solutions and supports a post-stripping interpretation. On this branch, ORFEO recovers the mostly west-to-east projected motion inferred from the H$\alpha$ morphology and is consistent with previous constraints on the interaction chronology. Requiring only $\sim10$--11 min of wall-clock time for NGC 4569, ORFEO provides a computationally inexpensive inverse framework for deriving orbital, tail, and ram-pressure histories that can guide tailored simulations and be extended to larger samples of stripped galaxies.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.14028.title: Constraints on Lorentz Invariance Violation from PeV Gamma Rays of Cygnus X-3 Observed by LHAASO
arxiv.org/abs/2611.14028.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.14028v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) has detected photons with energies up to 3.7 PeV from the binary system Cygnus X-3 during a flaring episode. The combination of such extreme photon energies and the large source distance provides a sensitive probe of Lorentz invariance violation (LIV). In superluminal LIV scenarios, high-energy photons can become unstable and rapidly decay, resulting in a sharp spectral cutoff. However, the observed hard intrinsic spectrum of Cygnus X-3 exhibits no evidence for such a feature. This absence enables us to place stringent constraints on LIV, with the second-order LIV energy scale constrained to be above 10^{-2}M_{pl}, improving previous limits by nearly an order of magnitude.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.14038.title: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays require metal-rich sources
arxiv.org/abs/2611.14038.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.14038v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The elemental composition of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) must be evaluated at a given rigidity rather than energy to compare with candidate elemental abundances, such as those of low-energy cosmic rays seeding the acceleration of UHECRs. We determine the UHECR composition from fits to Pierre Auger Observatory data and evaluate the resulting abundances at fixed rigidity. We identify two classes of solutions consistent with measurements above $10^{17.8}$ eV: one in which the hydrogen flux at Earth is dominated by secondary nucleons produced by photodisintegration of heavier nuclei in extragalactic photon fields, and a second in which this contribution is less pronounced. Only the latter, which yields a mixture of primary and secondary protons at Earth, allows a hydrogen abundance at the source comparable to that of low-energy cosmic rays. However, both classes of solutions require an overabundance of nuclei in the silicon-iron group. Other source models from the literature also fail to reproduce the full elemental composition. The metallicity of UHECRs thus differs markedly from that of all candidate seed populations considered, leaving the origin of the heavy-element excess unresolved.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.14086.title: Cosmic String Networks with Time-Varying Tension: Field-Theory Simulations and an Analytic Model
arxiv.org/abs/2611.14086.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.14086v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cosmic string networks are predicted in some early-Universe scenarios, and in certain models, the string tension becomes a function of time. Here, for the first time, we perform numerical field-theory simulations of cosmic string networks with time-varying tension in an expanding Universe. We use a modified Abelian-Higgs model in which the tension varies as a power law of the scale factor $a$, that is, $\mu \propto a^{-2m}$. We perform simulations on grids containing $8192^3$ grid points, with $m\in[-0.5,0.5]$, during radiation- and matter-dominated epochs. We find that, in our model, a string network forms only when the potential decreases more slowly than the amplitude of field oscillations redshifts due to the expansion of the Universe. Once formed, the network evolves according to the standard scaling behavior predicted by the velocity-dependent one-scale (VOS) model. To interpret these results, we compare the predictions of the VOS model with time-dependent tension to the asymptotic values obtained from the numerical simulations. Overall, we find good agreement between the numerical field-theory simulations and the calibrated VOS model. These results shed light on the evolution of cosmic string networks with time-varying tension and have potential implications for their observational signatures.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.14107.title: Two-component $\gamma$-Ray Structure from the CR Sources
arxiv.org/abs/2611.14107.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.14107v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: With the advent of a new generation of observational experiments and the accumulation of data, an increasing number of cosmic-ray sources have been found to exhibit pronounced two-component structures in their gamma-ray spectra above GeV energies. To investigate whether these structures share a common physical origin, we conduct a statistical study of sources exhibiting such features using a two-component model of cosmic-ray sources and examine their gamma-ray emission mechanisms. We find that the ambient environment significantly affects the spectral morphology. Sources located in low-density environments but surrounded by dense molecular clumps exhibit two clearly separated spectral peaks. In contrast, sources embedded in dense environments with additional dense molecular clumps nearby retain two-component spectral features, but the components overlap more smoothly, with the high-energy component appearing primarily as a relatively broad shoulder rather than a distinct peak.
