Sub‑Saharan Africa accounts for 45% of global snakebite deaths and envenomings.
Over 800,000 survivors suffer long‑term disabilities such as amputations.

co2_dataset_upgrade.headline: NASA’s OCO-2 and OCO-3 Data Upgrade Sharpens Decade‑Long CO₂ Record
co2_dataset_upgrade.summary: Updated algorithms for OCO-2 and OCO-3 produce a more accurate 2014‑2026 atmospheric CO₂ dataset that aligns closely with ground‑based measurements.
highlights: New processing algorithm improves instrument calibration and accounts for clouds, aerosols, and ocean reflectance
Revised record shows tighter agreement between OCO‑2, OCO‑3, and global ground‑based CO₂ networks
Monthly CO₂ accumulation can now be tracked, enabling near‑real‑time monitoring of extreme events

scientists_discover_why_chronic_back_pai.headline: Movement‑Triggered Back Pain Switches On Brain’s Self‑Identity Network
scientists_discover_why_chronic_back_pai.summary: A UC San Diego study finds that movement‑induced chronic low back pain activates the brain’s Default Mode Network, linking pain to personal identity.
highlights: 114 participants performed a leg raise test while arterial spin labeling fMRI recorded brain activity
During movement‑evoked pain the Default Mode Network became more active, opposite to acute pain responses
Stronger DMN‑somatosensory cortex connectivity correlated with higher pain severity
Researchers propose mindfulness meditation and psilocybin to decouple pain from self‑identity

interstellar_medium_map.headline: New 3‑D Map Reveals Unstable Interstellar Medium Around the Sun
interstellar_medium_map.summary: Combining Gaia dust data with a UV radiation map shows that about 41% of nearby interstellar space is in a thermally unstable state, challenging classic models.
highlights: The 2024 dust map spans a 4,000‑light‑year sphere centered on the Sun
UV radiation map from Stanford’s Troy Porter provides temperature information
Analysis finds 27% cold, 32% warm, and 41% unstable gas fractions
Authors argue the unstable fraction cannot be explained solely by map smoothing

new_dwarf_planet.headline: Rubin Observatory Spots Potential Sixth Dwarf Planet Beyond Pluto
highlights: Size estimate ranges from 600 to 1,500 km across, comparable to half Pluto’s diameter
Orbits the Sun at roughly 46 AU, just beyond Pluto’s 40 AU average distance
Shows a 7:12 orbital resonance with Neptune, similar to Haumea’s resonance
First detected in Rubin data on Oct 13 2026 and traced back to 2016 Dark Energy Camera images
If confirmed, would become the third‑largest known dwarf planet after Pluto and Eris

gamma_ray_burst_geometry.headline: Off‑Axis Jet Reveals Bright Afterglow in Unusual GRB 260310A
gamma_ray_burst_geometry.summary: A faint initial gamma flash followed by record‑breaking X‑ray, optical and radio afterglows in GRB 260310A is explained by an off‑axis two‑component jet.
highlights: GRB 260310A showed a weak one‑minute gamma flash then a slowly rising optical afterglow that outshone its host galaxy
Multi‑wavelength observations from Fermi, Chandra, XMM‑Newton, Einstein Probe, Large Binocular Telescope, VLA and Calar Alto
Researchers attribute the unusual light curve to an off‑axis view of a jet with distinct reverse‑shock and forward‑shock
The burst occurred at redshift z 0.153, linking it to a broad‑lined Type Ic supernova

radiation_shield_breach.headline: May 2024 Solar Superstorm Breached Earth’s “Impenetrable” Radiation Shield
radiation_shield_breach.summary: A May 2024 solar superstorm triggered local chorus waves that accelerated electrons to multi‑MeV energies inside the previously impenetrable Van Allen belt boundary.
highlights: Arase observed ultra‑relativistic electron fluxes 5,000 times above background at ~11,500 km altitude
Electron phase‑space‑density analysis showed a peak exactly where the protective barrier had existed
The depleted plasmasphere and negative ionospheric storm created conditions for efficient chorus‑wave acceleration
The enhanced radiation persisted for months until another storm in October 2024 reshaped the magnetosphere

crocodile_survival_astroid.headline: Warm‑Climate Preference Helped Crocodiles Survive the Dinosaur‑Killing Asteroid
crocodile_survival_astroid.summary: A new Science Advances analysis of over 7,000 fossils shows crocodile ancestors thrived in tropical refuges, escaping the harsh post‑impact conditions that doomed dinosaurs.
highlights: Crocodile lineages tracked warm climates for 250 million years, expanding into high latitudes during hot periods
Computer models of Earth’s climate 66 million years ago reveal equatorial refuges remained suitable after the Chicxulub impact
Study examined >7,000 fossils and >400 living and extinct species, confirming niche conservatism as key survival factor
Researchers warn modern habitat loss may hinder crocodiles’ historic strategy of moving toward suitable climates

neptune_trojan_asteroids_discovery.headline: Queen's Belfast Team Discovers Neptune's Elusive Trojan Asteroids
neptune_trojan_asteroids_discovery.summary: An international team led by Queen's University Belfast used Vera C.
highlights: Two asteroids and one candidate were confirmed as permanent members of Neptune's trailing Trojan cloud
The discovery was made using early LSST survey data from the 8.4‑meter Rubin telescope
Rubin’s nine‑year survey is expected to uncover tens to hundreds of additional Neptune Trojans

oxygen_nuclei_collisions_early_universe.headline: Oxygen Collisions at RHIC Reveal Quark‑Gluon Plasma in Small Systems
oxygen_nuclei_collisions_early_universe.summary: Scientists at Brookhaven’s RHIC have observed jet‑quenching in 200 GeV oxygen‑oxygen collisions, confirming quark‑gluon plasma formation in much smaller nuclei.
highlights: Jet‑quenching shows a 20% suppression of high‑energy particles in the oxygen collisions
The measurement uses data from the STAR detector collected in 2021
This is the lowest‑energy, smallest‑system observation of QGP to date

blood_test_alzheimers_risk.headline: Blood Test Measuring p‑tau217 Predicts Alzheimer’s Risk Up to a Decade Ahead
blood_test_alzheimers_risk.summary: A large international study found that high blood levels of p‑tau217 forecast a 38% chance of cognitive impairment within five years and up to 78% within ten years.
highlights: Researchers from Mass General Brigham Neuroscience Institute analyzed 2,684 cognitively normal adults across six cohorts in
Participants with the highest p‑tau217 levels faced a 38% five‑year and 78% ten‑year risk of developing cognitive impairment.
p‑tau217 predicted decline independently of amyloid‑beta PET findings and APOE4 genotype.

bacterial_defense_discovery.headline: Bacterial ‘type VI retron’ defense flips DNA switch to kill viruses
bacterial_defense_discovery.summary: Scientists at Gladstone Institutes uncovered a backward‑acting type VI retron that produces DNA only after phage infection, triggering a lethal toxin to stop viral spread.
highlights: Type VI retrons generate minimal DNA in healthy cells, then surge DNA production upon phage entry
The DNA surge releases an RNA block, allowing rapid synthesis of a small membrane‑disrupting toxin
Researchers used Spacer‑seq, a CRISPR‑Cas‑based method, to detect the low‑level DNA previously missed

metals_resist_deep_freeze.headline: Metals Defy Extreme Cold at -424°F via Hidden Twinning Mechanism
metals_resist_deep_freeze.summary: Scientists uncovered that niobium‑titanium alloys stay ductile at -253°C by activating nanoscale twinning, challenging long‑standing brittleness limits in materials.
highlights: Two experimental alloys of niobium and titanium remain damage‑tolerant at 20 K (-253°C).
Nanoscale twinning and phase transformation create new deformation pathways when dislocation motion stalls.
Tests were performed with the Engin‑X instrument at the ISIS Neutron and Muon Source using helium cooling.
The study appears in Nature and suggests design routes for cryogenic aerospace and energy components.

vitamin_a_discovery_vision.headline: Vitamin A and Thyroid Hormones Drive Foveola Cone Transformation in Human Retina
vitamin_a_discovery_vision.summary: Researchers at Johns Hopkins used retinal organoids to show retinoic acid and thyroid hormone reshape cone cells, revising a 30‑year‑old vision model.
highlights: Retinoic acid derived from vitamin A limits blue cone presence in the foveola during weeks 10‑12 of fetal development.
Thyroid hormone prompts remaining blue cones to convert into red and green cones by week 14.
The study, published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, used human retinal organoids to replace animal models.

ancient_meteorite_mars_wet_past.headline: Ancient Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001 Reveals Warm, Wet Pre‑Noachian Mars
ancient_meteorite_mars_wet_past.summary: New Science paper shows Teghaza 001 formed over 4.1 billion years ago, bearing water‑altered minerals and oxygen‑18 signatures indicating early Mars was warm and wet.
highlights: Teghaza 001 is a single‑type igneous rock dated to ≥4.1 billion years using U‑Pb zircon analysis
Oxygen‑18 and manganese‑oxide domains suggest interaction with surface fluids on early Mars
The meteorite’s composition differs from younger Martian meteorites, matching ancient crustal material
Researchers propose the sample originated from Mars’ Pre‑Noachian southern highlands

22k_year_old_human_dna_cave_dirt.headline: 22,000‑Year‑Old Human DNA Recovered From Spanish Cave Sediment
22k_year_old_human_dna_cave_dirt.summary: Scientists extracted nuclear DNA from a few grains of sediment in El Mirón Cave, revealing a western ancestry group and population continuity during the last ice age.
highlights: Sediment weighing only a few rice grains yielded enough DNA after 100 sequencing runs
The team sifted through over a billion DNA fragments to identify traces from multiple individuals
Genomic analysis shows western ancestry with dark skin, hair and eyes, and no major population replacement
Comparison with older French and Spanish genomes indicates limited eastern admixture before the last glacial maximum

data_driven_discovery_of_lunar_fe_bearin.headline: High‑Valence Fe Oxides Identified as Prime Lunar Water Reservoirs
data_driven_discovery_of_lunar_fe_bearin.summary: Machine‑learning models reveal that mixed‑valence Fe‑bearing oxides, especially magnetite, efficiently retain solar‑wind hydrogen and produce water in sunlit lunar regions.
highlights: Electronic‑structure‑informed XGBoost predicts H insertion and H₂O formation energies with high accuracy
Fe‑bearing oxides with Fe³⁺/Fe⁴⁺ states outperform Fe²⁺‑dominated lunar minerals
Eleven high‑/mixed‑valence oxides meet criteria for hydrogen retention, diffusion length <100 nm, and favorable H₂O/H₂ fugacity
Lunar magnetite emerges as the most promising candidate for in‑situ water production

ancient_ape_fossil_egypt.headline: Ancient Egyptian Ape Fossil Pushes Human Origins Northward
ancient_ape_fossil_egypt.summary: A 17‑ to 18‑million‑year‑old jaw of Masripithecus moghraensis from Wadi Moghra suggests early ape evolution may have begun in North Africa and the Middle East.
highlights: First definitive early Miocene ape fossil discovered in North Africa.
Species named Masripithecus moghraensis shows robust jaw and large teeth indicating a versatile fruit‑based diet.
Bayesian phylogenetic analysis links the fossil closer to living apes than any East African Miocene specimens.
Findings challenge the long‑standing view that ape ancestors originated primarily in East Africa.

cortex_wide_neuronal_dynamics_fmri.headline: Cortex-wide Calcium Waves Drive Resting‑State fMRI Quasi‑Periodic Patterns
cortex_wide_neuronal_dynamics_fmri.summary: Simultaneous wide‑field calcium imaging and fMRI reveal that slow cortical activity waves precisely precede and shape quasi‑periodic BOLD patterns during rest.
highlights: Time‑locked correlation found between calcium‑based neural QPPs and BOLD‑fMRI QPPs across the cortex
Wide‑field calcium imaging captured slow waves unfolding over seconds, matching fMRI spatiotemporal signatures
Study validates that BOLD QPPs originate from preceding neuronal activity rather than vascular artifacts
Research conducted with multimodal setup at Yale University’s Neurotechnology Core and MR Research Center

tree_muscle_discovery.headline: Trees Use Hidden ‘Muscle‑Like’ Wood to Straighten Themselves
tree_muscle_discovery.summary: Researchers found that trees sense their own shape and generate opposing tension wood, acting like muscles, to correct posture and stay upright.
highlights: Young poplar trees were grown on a rotating platform inside a uniformly lit sphere to isolate proprioception
Tension wood formed on the opposite side of the stem, creating counter‑pulling forces that straightened the curve
The study appears in New Phytologist (2026) with DOI 10.1111/nph.71238
Findings suggest new strategies for breeding straighter timber and lodging‑resistant crops

giant_virus_yields_potassium_channel_gen.headline: Giant Algal Virus Reveals Ancient Tandem Potassium Channel Gene
giant_virus_yields_potassium_channel_gen.summary: Scientists identified a functional two‑pore potassium channel gene in a marine algal virus, suggesting viral contributions to complex protein evolution.
highlights: The DNA virus infecting marine algae encodes a tandem K⁺ channel with functional properties.
Phylogenetic analysis shows the channel originated from the virus, not from host gene theft.
Findings support the idea that giant mimiviruses have driven the evolution of complex proteins in higher organisms.
The same virus also harbors a light‑controlled ion channel previously used in optogenetics.

conifers_southern_hemisphere_growth.headline: Southern Hemisphere Boosts Conifer Growth and Drought Resilience, Implications for Carbon Sinks
conifers_southern_hemisphere_growth.summary: A global study of 192 sites shows Northern‑hemisphere conifers grow up to four times faster and store more carbon when planted in the Southern Hemisphere.
highlights: Conifers grew up to four‑fold faster and showed higher carbohydrate reserves in Southern‑hemisphere sites.
Faster growth and drought tolerance were observed across pines, spruces, firs and cedars at 192 locations on four continents.
Researchers warn that non‑native plantations may invade native ecosystems and increase fire risk, especially in Brazil’s Cerrado
Native Southern beeches (Nothofagus) displayed comparable growth, offering a more sustainable afforestation option.

pesticide_parkinsons_risk.headline: Common pesticide chlorpyrifos raises Parkinson’s risk 2.5‑fold, study finds
pesticide_parkinsons_risk.summary: Long‑term residential exposure to chlorpyrifos was linked to more than 2.5 times higher odds of Parkinson’s disease in a UCLA cohort, and the toxin’s damage to neuronal autophagy was demonstrated in mice and zebrafish.
highlights: People with prolonged chlorpyrifos exposure had >2.5‑fold increased Parkinson’s risk (829 cases, 824 controls)
Mouse models showed dopamine‑neuron loss, movement deficits, inflammation, and alpha‑synuclein accumulation after inhalation
Zebrafish experiments identified disrupted autophagy as the mechanism and showed that restoring it protected neurons

large_field_single_cell_morphodynamic_sc.headline: Rapid Single‑Cell Scattering Imaging Cuts AST Time to 95 Minutes
large_field_single_cell_morphodynamic_sc.summary: A large‑field label‑free scattering platform quantifies single‑bacterial morphodynamics, delivering phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility results in about 95 minutes with 96.7 % agreement.
highlights: Large‑field scattering imaging monitors thousands of bacteria simultaneously
Deep‑learning segmentation extracts scattering intensity and geometric features during β‑lactam exposure
Distinct morphodynamic trajectories enable susceptibility calls within 60 minutes
Testing ten clinical blood cultures achieved 96.7 % categorical agreement with reference methods
Method resolves resistant subpopulations and estimates minimum inhibitory concentrations

ultrasound_nanoparticle_glioblastoma.headline: Focused Ultrasound and Nanoparticles Deliver microRNA Therapy Against Glioblastoma
ultrasound_nanoparticle_glioblastoma.summary: UVA researchers combined focused ultrasound, microbubble‑enabled blood‑brain barrier opening, and microRNA‑laden nanoparticles to suppress multiple glioblastoma genes in mice.
highlights: MicroRNAs targeting several oncogenic pathways slowed tumor growth in mouse models
Focused ultrasound guided by MRI temporarily opened the blood‑brain barrier for nanoparticle entry
The approach bypasses drug‑resistance issues by acting on genes without existing pharmaceuticals
Study results published in the Journal of Clinical Investigation (open‑access)

hidden_driver_high_cholesterol.headline: UC San Diego Researchers Identify Ral‑CTSA Pathway Driving LDL Receptor Loss
hidden_driver_high_cholesterol.summary: A hidden Ral‑dependent mechanism reduces LDL receptors, raising LDL cholesterol, and an existing cathepsin A inhibitor safely lowered LDL in mice.
highlights: High‑cholesterol diets activate Ral, triggering cathepsin A to degrade LDL receptors
Blocking cathepsin A stabilized receptors and cut circulating LDL dramatically in mice
The CTSA inhibitor has already passed a Phase 1 safety trial in humans
The discovery was published in Nature and targets a pathway distinct from statins and PCSK9 inhibitors

5.headline: Star Cluster Dynamics Delay Formation of Gaia Neutron‑Star Binaries
5.summary: Direct N‑body simulations show that Gaia‑detectable neutron‑star–main‑sequence binaries emerge only after black‑hole depletion in 10⁴ M⊙ clusters.
highlights: NS‑MS binaries meeting Gaia criteria appear post‑BH depletion
Black‑hole subsystem monopolizes strong encounters until it vanishes
Simulations model 10⁴ M⊙ clusters in a Galactic tidal field

arxiv_2610_41621v1.headline: ELT/ANDES Reveals Oxygen Detectability Varies Across Stellar Types
arxiv_2610_41621v1.summary: A new study shows that O₂ signatures are far easier to detect on planets orbiting M‑ and K‑dwarfs than on Sun‑like stars, especially for modern‑Earth analogues.
highlights: Modern‑Earth O₂ reaches 5σ detection in just 9 transits around an M3V star, but remains below 3σ for the Sun
Archean CH₄ requires 33–42 transits for a 5σ signal on a Sun‑like host, yet only 2–4 transits for oxygenated epochs around K2V
Across FGKM hosts, O₂ never attains 5σ for 3.9 Ga models, highlighting a strong contrast between anoxic and oxic atmospheres

2.headline: JWST NIRISS Spectroscopy Reveals Burstier Star Formation in Low‑Mass Galaxies
2.summary: JWST/NIRISS WFSS data in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field measure Hα and Hβ emission from 284 galaxies, showing increased scatter in the star‑forming main sequence at low masses.
highlights: 284 galaxies with >3σ Hα or Hβ detections were analyzed
Intrinsic scatter of the Hα‑based SFMS is 0.35‑0.5 dex, higher than UV‑based SFMS
FIRE simulations underpredict the observed scatter by up to 0.25 dex
Stellar masses as low as log(M/M☉)≈7 at z≈0.5 are probed

two_loop_matter_ps_2026.headline: Fast Two-Loop Matter Power Spectrum Computed with FFTLog and Kite Integrals
two_loop_matter_ps_2026.summary: A new FFTLog‑based method delivers millisecond‑speed two‑loop power spectrum calculations with ten‑digit precision for the EFTofLSS.
highlights: FFTLog decomposes the linear spectrum into complex power laws, turning two‑loop corrections into cosmology‑independent kite
Mellin–Barnes lattice summation achieves ~10⁻¹⁰ precision even for large imaginary powers
Precomputed matrices enable new‑cosmology evaluations in a few milliseconds with <10⁻⁴ relative error up to k=0.2 h Mpc⁻¹

icecube_detects_ghost_particles_with_10_.headline: IceCube Observatory Detects Ultra‑High‑Energy Neutrinos Ten Billion Times Solar Levels
icecube_detects_ghost_particles_with_10_.summary: Scientists at IceCube have recorded neutrinos with energies roughly ten billion times greater than solar neutrinos, opening a new window on cosmic extremes.
highlights: IceCube detected only a few dozen ultra‑high‑energy neutrinos each year, each carrying ~10 billion times solar neutrino energy.
The observatory uses photomultiplier tubes embedded in one cubic kilometre of clear Antarctic ice to capture Cherenkov light
UC San Diego researchers, including George Fuller and Francis Halzen, link these detections to probing the origins of

volcanic_thermostat.headline: Tropical Volcanoes Drive Most Northern Hemisphere Cooling, Study Finds
volcanic_thermostat.summary: New modeling and tree‑ring analysis show tropical eruptions cool the Northern Hemisphere more often than rarer extratropical eruptions.
highlights: NASA climate model simulations found extratropical eruptions boost cooling at most two‑fold, not the previously claimed 7.5‑fold.
Tree‑ring records from 1783 Iceland, 536 CE mid‑latitudes, and 43 BCE Alaska confirm tropical eruptions correlate with stronger
Aerosol lifespans average nine months for extratropical eruptions versus up to three years for tropical eruptions.

ultrathin_kagome_material.headline: Ultrathin 2D kagome material enables high‑temperature flat‑band studies
ultrathin_kagome_material.summary: Researchers at Seoul National University have created a monolayer kagome crystal A2T3X4 that hosts tunable flat‑band electrons, opening a platform for exotic quantum phenomena.
highlights: The new van der Waals kagome compound A₂T₃X₄ can be exfoliated into atomically thin layers by mechanical cleavage.
Nano‑ARPES measurements reveal a flat electronic band near the Fermi level with electron density ~1 nm⁻², two orders of
Many‑body calculations predict fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect (FQAHE) emerging at 14–29 meV, an order of magnitude

single_molecule_quantum_networks.headline: Molecular Qubits Achieve Stable Spin‑Photon Interface for Future Quantum Networks
single_molecule_quantum_networks.summary: Researchers at NVision Quantum Technologies demonstrated that individual carbene molecules can store quantum information for 2.2 ms and emit stable light for over an hour, paving the way for scalable quantum networks.
highlights: Controlled and read out the spin state of a single carbene molecule
Achieved spin coherence of approximately 2.2 milliseconds
Maintained emission frequency stability for more than one hour
Operated the system at 4.5 Kelvin using laser excitation
Demonstrated compatibility with thin‑film photonic chip integration

melting_permafrost_has_birthed_a_new_typ.headline: New Permafrost Detachment Slides Reveal Climate‑Driven Catastrophic Landslides
melting_permafrost_has_birthed_a_new_typ.summary: Scientists identified a novel class of landslides where thawing permafrost detaches, driven by past wildfires and warming, causing massive earth movement in Canada.
highlights: The 2018 slide displaced 18 million m³ of frozen ground, damming the Redstone River.
Field and satellite data show sliding surfaces ~20 m below ground and decades of slow creep before failure.
Simulations indicate wildfire‑heated cracks allow water to thaw permafrost from below, triggering detachment.

lhc_quark_gluon_plasma_small_collisions.headline: CERN's LHC Finds Quark‑Gluon Plasma in Small Oxygen and Neon Collisions
lhc_quark_gluon_plasma_small_collisions.summary: Scientists at CERN report that collisions of oxygen and neon nuclei at the Large Hadron Collider recreate the primordial quark‑gluon plasma, previously thought exclusive to heavy ions.
highlights: ATLAS observed jet energy loss in central oxygen‑oxygen and neon‑neon collisions, indicating parton energy loss in the medium.
CMS measured suppressed charged‑particle production in oxygen‑oxygen and neon‑neon events compared with proton‑proton collisions.
ALICE confirmed parton energy loss by comparing neutral‑pion yields in oxygen‑oxygen versus proton‑oxygen collisions.
LHCb reported stronger suppression of charm‑containing particles in neon collisions, consistent with larger plasma volumes.

stem_cells_in_deep_sleep_may_point_to_a_.institution: German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) and HI‑STEM Stem Cell Institute
stem_cells_in_deep_sleep_may_point_to_a_.headline: Deep‑sleep blood stem cells discovered as lifelong reserve in mice
stem_cells_in_deep_sleep_may_point_to_a_.summary: Researchers identified EPCR‑positive, CD150‑negative blood stem cells that stay dormant for months, preserving regenerative capacity throughout a mouse’s life.
highlights: The EPCR‑positive, CD150‑negative cells remain quiescent for over 200 days, far longer than conventional stem cells
About 10%‑15% of these cells retain a quiescence marker versus ~2% of typical stem cells
These deep‑sleep cells preferentially differentiate into immune cells, especially lymphocytes
Single‑cell transplants showed they can reconstitute all blood lineages and sustain them lifelong

low_temp_ammonia_synthesis.headline: Barium‑based Antiperovskite Catalyst Enables Low‑Temp Ammonia Production
low_temp_ammonia_synthesis.summary: A new Ba₃AlO₄₋ₓNᵧHz/Co catalyst synthesised on Al₂O₃ nanorods produces ammonia at 300 °C and 0.9 MPa, outperforming Ru and Fe benchmarks.
highlights: Catalyst achieves 15.9 mmol g⁻¹ h⁻¹ NH₃ synthesis rate under mild conditions
Molecular (N₂)⁻ ions at Co‑Ba‑Al interfaces weaken the N≡N bond
Hierarchical anti‑perovskite structure stabilises active nitrogen species
Study published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society, peer‑reviewed

ryugu_contradiction_solution.institution: Various research institutions (University of Tokyo et al.)
ryugu_contradiction_solution.headline: M‑S‑H Discovery Resolves Ryugu Mineral Matrix Contradiction
ryugu_contradiction_solution.summary: New synchrotron analysis of Ryugu samples reveals poorly crystalline magnesium silicate hydrate, explaining dual mineral signatures without separate aqueous alteration events.
highlights: Ryugu matrix contains abundant poorly crystalline M‑S‑H alongside minor serpentine and saponite
Study used SPring‑8 and Photon Factory High Energy Accelerator x‑ray facilities in Japan
M‑S‑H’s flexible Mg‑Si ratios allow it to form before and transform into clay‑like minerals
Findings suggest carbonaceous chondrite matrices can vary compositionally without distinct water environments

generic_hiv_prevention_shot.headline: FDA Grants Tentative Approval for Generic HIV Prevention Shot
generic_hiv_prevention_shot.summary: The FDA gave tentative approval to Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories to produce a generic lenacapavir injectable, aiming to lower costs for low‑ and middle‑income countries.
highlights: Generic lenacapavir will be priced at about $40 per person annually
The shot provides near‑complete HIV protection with a single dose every six months
Dr. Reddy’s plans to begin shipments next month to expand global access

scientists_reverse_liver_cell_aging_and_.headline: Experimental drug cinaciguat rejuvenates aging liver cells, halves amyloid‑beta and normalizes LDL in rats
scientists_reverse_liver_cell_aging_and_.summary: USC researchers showed that a two‑week cinaciguat regimen restored aged liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, cutting circulating amyloid‑beta by 50% and returning bad cholesterol to youthful levels.
highlights: Cinaciguat reopened microscopic pores in liver sinusoidal endothelial cells of older rats
Amyloid‑beta concentrations fell approximately 50%, matching levels in young animals
Low‑density lipoprotein levels dropped to youthful concentrations despite expectations
The treatment reactivated soluble guanylate cyclase‑HB‑EGF signaling between liver cells

single_measurement_qubit_error_reduction.institution: University of Regensburg and international partners
single_measurement_qubit_error_reduction.headline: Single Pre‑Measurement Halves Error Rate in Superconducting Qubits
single_measurement_qubit_error_reduction.summary: Researchers at University of Regensburg added a rapid frequency check before operations, cutting qubit error rates from 0.14% to 0.065% in a superconducting circuit.
highlights: A single pre‑measurement identifies the active resonance frequency of a bistable qubit
Real‑time feedback adjusts control signals, reducing average error rate by about 54%
Maximum observed error reduction reaches 77% compared with no feedback
Technique demonstrated on a superconducting circuit at the Israeli Quantum Computing Center

plant_immune_memory_nature_communication.headline: Plant Immune Memory Offers New Epigenetic Path for Crop Breeding
plant_immune_memory_nature_communication.summary: Researchers at the University of Sheffield used a ROS1‑based vaccination tool to reveal how plants store and reset immune memory, opening routes for epigenetic crop improvement.
highlights: ROS1 removes DNA methylation tags, creating lasting epigenetic immune memory
XVE:ROS1 enables controlled activation of ROS1 without destabilising transposons
Epigenetic changes induced in rice persist partially across generations, suggesting heritable traits

bee_nest_plastic_inspiration.institution: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
bee_nest_plastic_inspiration.headline: Bee‑Made Polyester Offers Blueprint for Soil‑Degrading Plastics
bee_nest_plastic_inspiration.summary: Researchers found that the polyester lining of Colletes inaequalis nests loses up to half its weight in soil within four months, suggesting a model for fast‑degrading plastics.
highlights: Nest linings composed of a polyethylene‑like polyester degraded from 73% to 40% of original weight in four months of natural
Material remained flexible initially but became brittle and crumbled after eleven months, mirroring single‑use plastic lifecycles.
Crystalline content (~60%) was poorly organized and contained enzymes that can cleave ester bonds, possibly driving rapid

jwst_heavy_black_hole_seeds.headline: JWST Identifies Dense Star Clusters as Birthplaces of Heavy Black Hole Seeds
jwst_heavy_black_hole_seeds.summary: JWST observations of the Cosmic Gems and Firefly Sparkle galaxies reveal dense, metal‑poor young massive clusters that can produce intermediate‑mass black holes of up to thousand solar masses.
highlights: The Cosmic Gems arc at redshift z ∼ 10.2 hosts five young massive clusters with masses 10⁵–10⁷ M⊙ and radii ~0.4 pc, yielding
The Firefly Sparkle galaxy at redshift z ∼ 8.3 contains ten clusters of larger radii (4–6 pc), producing smaller IMBHs of
Low metallicity (Z ≲ 0.02 Z⊙) in these clusters limits stellar‑wind mass loss, enabling runaway collisions to grow heavy
Analytic collision models were validated against direct N‑body simulations, confirming the plausibility of IMBH formation in

sea_level_rise_economic_toll.headline: Sea‑Level Rise Threatens $100 Billion‑Year Ecosystem Services by 2100
sea_level_rise_economic_toll.summary: A new global accounting predicts sea‑level rise could erase over 100 billion international dollars of ecosystem services annually by the end of the century.
highlights: Losses total 164.46 billion Int$2020 per year under the “Middle of the Road” scenario
Wetlands face the highest relative loss, up to 2.20% of their extent
Absolute value losses peak in China, Myanmar, Brazil, Russia and Vietnam

rare_beauty_particle_decay.headline: LHCb Finds First Evidence of Ultra‑Rare Beauty‑Quark Decay
rare_beauty_particle_decay.summary: Physicists at CERN's upgraded LHCb experiment have observed the Bd→μμ decay, a process expected only once in ten billion beauty particles, reaching 3.2 σ significance.
highlights: Evidence of Bd→μμ decay observed with 3.2 σ statistical significance
Decay occurs roughly once in every 10 billion beauty particles
Upgraded LHCb can collect data five times faster thanks to new silicon pixel Vertex Locator
The result aligns with Standard Model predictions but opens a path to probe the Zeptoverse

lab_grown_neurons_3d_genome.headline: Lab‑grown neurons keep embryonic chromatin traits, study finds
lab_grown_neurons_3d_genome.summary: Researchers mapped over 300 3D genomes and found iPSC‑derived neurons retain progenitor‑like chromatin organization, differing from mature adult brain cells.
highlights: Compared 62 human and 34 mouse samples across stem, progenitor, fetal, and adult neurons
iPSC‑derived neurons show smaller, densely packed structural domains typical of early development
Repressive long‑range contacts are markedly reduced in lab‑grown neurons

mandrill_miscarriage.institution: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology / University of Turku
mandrill_miscarriage.headline: Pregnant Mandrills More Likely to Miscarry When Nursing Infant
mandrill_miscarriage.summary: In a wild Gabonese mandrill population, females nursing an infant faced higher fetal loss, linking maternal trade‑offs to reproductive timing.
highlights: Fetal loss occurred more often when mothers were simultaneously nursing a dependent infant.
Infant distress vocalizations and alpha male takeovers further increased miscarriage risk.
Females who lost a pregnancy conceived again sooner and ultimately produced similar numbers of surviving offspring.
The 11‑year study documented 356 pregnancies across 117 females, with 52 instances of fetal loss.

extracellular_vesicles_platform.institution: Germans Trias i Pujol Research Institute (IGTP) / Blood and Tissue Bank (BST)
extracellular_vesicles_platform.headline: Semiautomated GMP Platform Produces Consistent Extracellular Vesicle Batches for Regenerative Therapy
extracellular_vesicles_platform.summary: Researchers at IGTP and BST validated a semiautomated GMP‑compliant system that reliably generates extracellular vesicles from umbilical‑cord mesenchymal stromal cells.
highlights: Platform integrates bioreactor culture with tangential flow filtration and size‑exclusion chromatography.
Produced vesicle preparations meet GMP quality standards and show batch‑to‑batch consistency.
Uses chemically defined, animal‑free media for umbilical‑cord mesenchymal stromal cells.
Validated in iScience, paving way for cardiovascular regenerative trials.

ancient_star_collisions_jwst_red_dots.headline: Early Star Collisions May Explain Little Red Dots and Fast‑Growing Black Holes
ancient_star_collisions_jwst_red_dots.summary: Simulations show dense early‑universe star clusters merging into ultra‑massive stars, seeding intermediate‑mass black holes and accounting for mysterious Little Red Dots.
highlights: Dense star clusters in the early universe experience frequent stellar collisions
Repeated mergers can create a single star as massive as an entire cluster
Such ultra‑massive stars collapse into intermediate‑mass black holes, seeding supermassive black holes
The model links the disappearance of Little Red Dots to the cooling and expansion of the cosmos

lorentz_invariance_neutrinos.headline: KM3NeT Neutrino Telescope Finds No Lorentz Violation in Mediterranean Deep
lorentz_invariance_neutrinos.summary: Analyzing 5,828 atmospheric neutrinos with KM3NeT/ORCA, researchers set new limits on Lorentz invariance violation, including first direct constraints on muon‑tau neutrino differences.
highlights: Study used 1.4 years of data from six KM3NeT/ORCA detection units.
No Lorentz invariance violation observed, tightening previous bounds.
First direct limits placed on muon‑tau neutrino oscillation violations.
Results comparable to IceCube and Super‑Kamiokande despite early detector stage.

southern_ocean_nutrient_pathways.headline: Southern Ocean Waters Follow Distinct Nutrient Paths on Decades‑Long Northward Journey
southern_ocean_nutrient_pathways.summary: Researchers tracked Subantarctic Mode Water and Antarctic Intermediate Water using CFC ages, revealing differing nitrate, phosphate and silicate regeneration that shape global phytoplankton.
highlights: SAMW regenerates nitrate and phosphate faster than AAIW
AAIW releases silicate more rapidly, favoring diatom growth
CFC signatures provide decadal age estimates for water masses
Study links Southern Ocean physics to worldwide primary production

mit_crystal_structures_break_20_year_rul.headline: MIT Breaks 20‑Year Rule with Flexible Links to Forge New Nanoparticle Crystals
mit_crystal_structures_break_20_year_rul.summary: Researchers at MIT used highly flexible, charged molecular ligands to assemble nanoparticles into crystal structures never observed before, challenging two decades of rigid‑link dogma.
highlights: Flexible polymer ligands with opposite charges enable nanoparticles to self‑organize into open superlattices.
Adjusting particle size and ligand length controls the number of bonds each particle forms.
The method produced crystal lattices previously unseen in nanoparticle assembly.
Findings will appear in Nature Materials, opening routes to designer materials for electronics, medicine and energy.

altermagnetism_discovery.headline: SLAC Confirms Existence of Altermagnetism, a Third Magnetic Phase
altermagnetism_discovery.summary: Using circularly polarized X‑rays at ESRF, SLAC scientists experimentally verified altermagnetism in MnTe, revealing a magnetic class that merges ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic traits.
highlights: Circularly polarized X‑rays detected a chiral scattering signature unique to altermagnets.
MnTe, long thought to be an antiferromagnet, shows the defining chirality of altermagnetism.
The discovery bridges the stability of antiferromagnets with the spin‑current efficiency of ferromagnets.
Results were published in Science (2026) after reproducible measurements in 2024‑2025.

capture_free_telemetry_autonomous_gps_co.headline: Capture‑Free GPS Collars Let Wild Animals Tag Themselves
capture_free_telemetry_autonomous_gps_co.summary: A new autonomous system lets red deer, foxes and other wildlife self‑attach GPS collars, eliminating the need for stressful capture during research.
highlights: Capture‑Free Telemetry (CFT) deploys baited units that animals trigger to fit a collar around their neck
Field trials in Norway successfully fitted collars to red deer (Cervus elaphus) and red foxes (Vulpes vulpes)
Collars auto‑adjust, detach after weeks, and include safety weak spots to prevent entanglement
The method promises larger sample sizes and reduced behavioral bias compared with traditional capture‑based telemetry

id15.headline: Virtual Lifeless Earth Model Helps Distinguish Habitable from Inhabited Exoplanets
id15.summary: Researchers at the University of Washington created a life‑free Earth simulation that reproduces pre‑industrial conditions, offering a benchmark for the Habitable Worlds Observatory to spot false biosignature signals.
highlights: The coupled interior‑atmosphere model reproduces 19 key pre‑industrial Earth observations within uncertainties.
Synthetic reflected‑light spectra cover 0.2–2.0 µm, including CO2, H2O, O2, O3 and CH4 features.
The tool can be customized with albedo and atmospheric CO2 inputs to test any Earth‑like exoplanet.
Model predicts long‑term habitability without life, addressing false‑positive challenges for upcoming telescopes.

tiny_squeeze_changes_magnetism_altermagn.headline: Tiny Mechanical Squeeze Switches Magnetism in Altermagnets
tiny_squeeze_changes_magnetism_altermagn.summary: Applying a modest uniaxial pressure to altermagnet crystals dramatically reshapes their magnetic domains and alters the anomalous Hall effect, researchers report.
highlights: Mechanical strain changes magnetic domain populations in MnTe and FeS crystals
Neutron diffraction at ORNL's Spallation Neutron Source captured the magnetic restructuring
Strain‑tuned anomalous Hall effect reveals new routes for spintronic device control

accelerating_sea_level_rise_ireland.headline: Irish Sea Levels Accelerate Sharply Over Past Century, Study Finds
accelerating_sea_level_rise_ireland.summary: A century‑long reconstruction shows sea‑level rise around Ireland has accelerated since 2000, reaching rates several times higher than the 20th‑century average.
highlights: Current sea‑level rise rates around Ireland are the highest recorded in the past 100 years.
The study combined tide‑gauge records from six sites, adding newly digitized data from Cork, Tarbert and Galway.
Acceleration mirrors global sea‑level trends observed since the 1990s, but local variations persist.

event6.headline: Chiral Topological Phases Discovered in Disordered Amorphous Metals
event6.summary: Researchers show that local chirality can sustain topological semimetal behavior in amorphous metals, overturning the belief that disorder destroys such phases.
highlights: Local chirality order persists in amorphous structures, enabling robust topological states
Benjamin Wieder and Adolfo Grushin used symmetry group theory to reveal the hidden order
The study appears in Physical Review Materials and is also on arXiv

alphafold3_immune_prediction.institution: Translational Genomics Research Institute (TGen) / City of Hope
alphafold3_immune_prediction.headline: AlphaFold 3 Predicts TCR Antigen Specificity From Sequence Alone
alphafold3_immune_prediction.summary: Researchers at TGen used AlphaFold 3 to model MHC‑peptide‑TCR complexes from protein sequences, accurately forecasting T cell recognition of novel antigens.
highlights: AlphaFold 3 accurately reproduced known MHC:peptide:TCR structures
The model correctly predicted TCR recognition for eight tuberculosis‑derived MHC class II antigens
Prediction relies solely on genetic sequences, eliminating the need for experimental structure determination

molecular_imaging_reveals_how_shape_shif.institution: Kanazawa University / National Institute of Genetics
molecular_imaging_reveals_how_shape_shif.headline: High‑speed AFM captures shape‑shifting Smc5/6 protein binding DNA
molecular_imaging_reveals_how_shape_shif.summary: Researchers used high‑speed atomic force microscopy to visualize Smc5/6 adopting open and closed shapes that capture and tether DNA, revealing mechanisms of chromosome maintenance.
highlights: Smc5/6 alternates between I‑shaped and O‑shaped conformations driven by ATP binding
HS‑AFM recordings show Smc5/6 capturing DNA at its ends and within its arm cavity
The complex can tether two separate DNA segments, promoting DNA compaction
Observations were made with purified Smc5/6 from budding yeast in vitro

event10.headline: Light‑Driven Winds Explain Bright Galaxies Seen by JWST
event10.summary: Simulations show ultraviolet Lyman‑alpha radiation can blow low‑density gas and dust out of early galaxies, clearing the view and making them appear unusually bright.
highlights: Researchers at Flatiron Institute and University of Texas at Dallas used a 2.5‑million‑year simulation to calculate Lyman‑alpha
In low‑density regions, Lyman‑alpha photons repeatedly scatter, generating enough force to launch gas at high speeds.
The resulting “leaf‑blower” effect removes obscuring material, increasing the observed brightness of galaxies a few hundred
Findings are published in The Astrophysical Journal (2026) and represent a peer‑reviewed advance in early‑universe galaxy

ancient_dna_germanic_celtic.headline: Ancient DNA Reveals Unexpected Baltic Origins of Germanic and Celtic Languages
ancient_dna_germanic_celtic.summary: By sequencing 712 ancient genomes and comparing them with 4,009 others, researchers show Baltic migrations spread Germanic languages and a westward movement spread Celtic tongues.
highlights: Sequenced 712 new Iron Age genomes and integrated them with 4,009 existing samples
Identified a migration from the Baltic region (Finland‑northeastern Sweden) into southern Scandinavia around 800 years before
Demonstrated a westward Urnfield‑culture migration ~3,000 years ago that likely carried Celtic languages across Europe

global_les_220m.headline: Global Storm Models Reach 220‑Meter Resolution on Fugaku Supercomputer
highlights: Resolution increased from 3.5 km to 220 m, diminishing the popcorn‑like precipitation pattern.
Two turbulence schemes were tested, showing consistent cloud‑cover reduction at finer scales.
The study demonstrates that 220‑meter global large‑eddy simulations are now feasible on current supercomputers.
Authors note that improving turbulence parameterizations is essential for realistic cloud representation.

2611_06549v1.headline: Rare Substellar Companions Survive Common‑Envelope Evolution Around White Dwarfs
2611_06549v1.summary: A new population‑synthesis study predicts that up to 0.16% of white dwarfs host close substellar companions that survive common‑envelope phases, especially during thermal pulses.
highlights: Survival occurs only for companions engulfed during the thermally pulsing asymptotic‑giant branch.
Predicted orbital periods are a few hours, making transits geometrically rare.
Infrared excess from all survivors would be detectable with JWST out to 50 pc.
Occurrence rates translate to at most 2.53 companions within 50 pc of the Sun.

searching_for_signatures_of_i_process_nu.headline: Metal‑Rich Barium Stars Reveal i‑process Signatures Near Solar Metallicity
searching_for_signatures_of_i_process_nu.summary: New spectroscopic analysis of six metal‑rich barium stars shows extreme lead and europium enhancements, with two stars best explained by i‑process nucleosynthesis.
highlights: Three stars exhibit [Pb/Fe] up to +2.5 dex, among the highest recorded in metal‑rich giants
Two stars display [Eu/Fe] exceeding +1.1 dex, a rare trait for such metallicities
Abundance patterns in two objects conflict with standard s‑process models but match i‑process predictions
Findings suggest metal‑rich AGB stars also contribute elements traditionally linked to the r‑process

2611_05740v1.headline: 3D Simulations Reveal Stellar Convection Masks M‑dwarf Exoplanet Signals
2611_05740v1.summary: Using 3D radiation‑hydrodynamics models, researchers show that convection on M dwarfs can mimic or obscure atmospheric signatures of planets like GJ 3470 b in high‑resolution spectra.
highlights: Synthetic spectra from 3D radiative hydrodynamical simulations match observed K‑band data for GJ 3470 only modestly due to
Centre‑to‑limb variations and the Rossiter‑McLaughlin effect produce signals comparable to those of the transiting Neptune‑size
Principal component analysis can de‑trend stellar noise, but its success depends on the simultaneous presence of telluric and

dynamics_of_self_gravitating_halos_with_.headline: Decaying Dark Matter Heats Halos, Alters Density Profiles, Study Finds
dynamics_of_self_gravitating_halos_with_.summary: Researchers use the NSphere simulation to show that modest kick velocities from decaying dark matter puff out self‑gravitating halos, reshaping their density profiles.
highlights: NSphere code simulated halos over a wide range of decay times and kick velocities
If kick velocity is much smaller than the halo’s characteristic speed, the halo stays bound but expands
Anisotropic initial conditions produce noticeable changes in the final density profile
An emulator was trained to map decay parameters to relaxed halo profiles
Upcoming surveys could detect the halo‑scale signatures of decaying dark matter

chex_mate_density_profile_reconstruction.headline: CHEX-MATE Shows Azimuthal Median Recovers True Cluster Gas Densities
chex_mate_density_profile_reconstruction.summary: Using 109 simulated clusters observed from 40 sightlines, the CHEX-MATE study finds azimuthal median deprojection yields unbiased gas density profiles between 0.15 and 1.3 R₅₀₀.
highlights: Azimuthal median profiles have negligible bias across 0.15‑1.3 R₅₀₀
Mean profiles are biased by substructures unless clumps are carefully masked
Mean‑to‑median density ratio traces projected gas inhomogeneities but with limited precision for single clusters
Combining mean and median methods offers the most complete analysis for large X‑ray cluster surveys

desi_mw_emdf.headline: DESI Halo Stars Pinpoint Milky Way Mass and Concentration
desi_mw_emdf.summary: Using a data‑driven empirical distribution function on DESI DR2 halo stars, researchers measured the Milky Way’s virial mass and concentration with unprecedented precision.
highlights: RR Lyrae stars give log M_200c/M_⊙ = 12.15 +0.22/‑0.14 and log c_200c = 1.16 +0.09/‑0.12.
Combined with satellite dynamics, the final Milky Way halo mass is log M_200c/M_⊙ = 12.12 ±0.05 and concentration log c_200c =

human_evolution_interbreeding_400kyr.headline: Ancient Homo erectus Teeth Reveal Genetic Link to Modern Southeast Asians
human_evolution_interbreeding_400kyr.summary: Proteins extracted from 400,000‑year‑old Homo erectus teeth show interbreeding with Denisovans, leaving detectable genetic traces in present‑day Southeast Asian populations.
highlights: Six enamel protein samples from Zhoukoudian, Hexian and Sunjiadong dated to ~400,000 years were analyzed.
All specimens share a unique amino‑acid variant also found in Denisovan proteins.
The variant appears in modern genomes at ~21% frequency in the Philippines and ~1% in India.
Study published in Nature demonstrates that Homo erectus contributed genetic material to later human lineages.

scientists_discover_clogged_filter_revol.headline: Clogged Filter Membrane Could Slash Oil Refining Energy Use by One‑Third
scientists_discover_clogged_filter_revol.summary: Researchers at KAIST and Georgia Tech created a porous polyacrylonitrile membrane that separates crude oil at room temperature, promising up to 31.6% energy savings.
highlights: Uncoated PAN membrane forms sub‑2 nm channels as oil fouls the pores, enabling selective passage of lighter fractions
Achieves permeation rates ~23 times higher than previous crude‑oil membranes and operates stably for 28 days
Simulations predict 31.6% lower energy consumption, 37.6% fewer CO₂ emissions, and 36% reduced operating costs

hidden_immune_defense_discovery.headline: Hidden Enzyme Unveiled: 5-oxoETE Pathway Shields Cells from Inflammation
hidden_immune_defense_discovery.summary: Researchers at Memorial Sloan Kettering identified the DHRS7 enzyme, revealing that the 5-oxoETE signaling pathway both summons immune cells and protects healthy tissue from inflammatory damage.
highlights: The missing human gene DHRS7 was pinpointed using zebrafish, which retain the 5-oxoETE receptor absent in mice.
Disabling DHRS7 or its receptor hcar1-4 in zebrafish unexpectedly increased intestinal inflammation, indicating a protective role.
The pathway’s shield function involves NUDIX hydrolases that mitigate chemical stress from normal gut bacteria.
Findings, published in Nature, suggest targeting the 5-oxoETE system could aid treatments for cancer, IBD and asthma.

jwst_digital_twin_exoplanet_detection.headline: JWST’s New ‘Digital Twin’ Method Reveals Hidden Exoplanet 51 Eridani b
jwst_digital_twin_exoplanet_detection.summary: A physics‑based machine‑learning technique called FLIP models JWST’s minute imperfections, enabling starlight subtraction that uncovers the previously invisible planet 51 Eridani b.
highlights: FLIP combines a differentiable instrument model with wavefront sensing data to achieve PSF fidelity beyond JWST’s stability limit.
The method improves sensitivity by 2–15× over standard KLIP processing, delivering a >5 σ detection of 51 Eridani b at 4.3 µm.
Developed by Rodrigo Ferrer‑Chavez and Jason Wang at Northwestern University, the technique was published in Nature (2026).
FLIP’s “digital twin” approach could relax stability requirements for future missions like the Habitable Worlds Observatory.

cemetery_climate_disease_link.headline: Cemetery Teeth Reveal Climate’s Role in Industrial‑Era Rickets
cemetery_climate_disease_link.summary: Analysis of 30 teeth from Coach Lane shows childhood vitamin D deficiency spiked after volcanic eruptions during the Little Ice Age.
highlights: 30 teeth from 21 individuals examined for dentin mineralization failures
236 burials uncovered from the 1711‑1829 Coach Lane Quaker cemetery
91 of 109 individuals with known birth years were born within ten years of major volcanic eruptions
Research published in Frontiers in Environmental Archaeology (peer‑reviewed)

microbial_growth_simulated_mars_conditio.headline: Halophilic Microbe Grows Under Simulated Martian Subsurface Conditions
microbial_growth_simulated_mars_conditio.summary: A University of Florida experiment shows Haloferax volcanii can reproduce over months in low‑pressure, high‑salt, perchlorate‑rich conditions mimicking Mars’s shallow subsurface.
highlights: Microbe reproduced for 160 days in oxygen‑free, CO₂‑rich atmosphere
Growth required nitrate or perchlorate as electron acceptors
Dense biofilms formed, retaining water in the salty solution
Growth was slower than at Earth’s atmospheric pressure

ice_age_abrupt_climate_shifts_were_not_a.headline: Abrupt Ice‑Age Climate Shifts Took Centuries, Not Decades, Study Finds
ice_age_abrupt_climate_shifts_were_not_a.summary: High‑resolution speleothem records from China and India show that Dansgaard–Oeschger ocean circulation recoveries lasted about 180 years, far longer than previously thought.
highlights: Annual‑laminated speleothems from Cherrapunji and Shuixi Caves reveal transition durations averaging ~180 years.
Isotope‑enabled Earth system models identify a two‑stage AMOC recovery, with initial rapid sea‑ice retreat followed by slower
Greenland ice‑core δ¹⁸O records reflect only the first rapid stage, explaining the discrepancy with Asian speleothem data.
Findings suggest future AMOC tipping could unfold over centuries, reshaping risk assessments.

active_volcanoes_mars.headline: Active Volcanoes Detected on Mars Linked to HCl Emissions
active_volcanoes_mars.summary: Scientists have correlated hydrogen chloride gas detections with fresh fissures in Alba Mons, suggesting ongoing volcanic activity on Mars.
highlights: ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter recorded 15 instances of HCl in 2019
Narrow fissures in Alba Mons were matched to those gas releases
Team modeled turbulent wind conditions to link emissions to underground lava flow

id_7.institution: Tohoku University & Japan Atomic Energy Agency (JAEA)
id_7.headline: Electric Current Switches Quantum‑Geometric Nonlinear Hall State in Mn₃Sn Magnet
id_7.summary: Researchers at Tohoku University and JAEA electrically toggled the quantum‑geometric nonlinear Hall response in Mn₃Sn by using spin‑orbit torque pulses.
highlights: Observed third‑order Hall voltage proportional to current³ at room temperature in epitaxial Mn₃Sn films.
Demonstrated reversible sign switching of the QgNLH response using opposite‑polarity current pulses.
Spin‑orbit torque from an adjacent heavy‑metal layer drives magnetic‑order switching, enabling on‑demand control.
Findings published in Newton (Nov 4 2026) and suggest routes to electrically tunable nonlinear devices.

dna_nanoswitches_find_new_drug_leads_fas.institution: Wyss Institute at Harvard University, Boston Children’s Hospital, Harvard Medical School
dna_nanoswitches_find_new_drug_leads_fas.headline: DNA Nanoswitch Platform Accelerates Drug Lead Discovery by Targeting Protein Interactions
dna_nanoswitches_find_new_drug_leads_fas.summary: The new FIND platform uses DNA nanoswitches to screen a 400‑million‑compound library, rapidly identifying molecules that modulate disease‑relevant protein‑protein interactions.
highlights: FIND screened a 400‑million‑member DNA‑encoded library to find modulators of PPAR‑gamma/CBP interaction
A nanobody that alters SARS‑CoV‑2 spike binding was discovered using the same method
The approach recovered a known beta‑2 adrenergic receptor activator as a validation control
DNA nanoswitches toggle between linear and looped states, enabling gel‑based separation of active compounds

early_galaxies_bright_jwst.headline: Lyman‑Alpha Radiation Clears Gas, Brightening Early Star Clusters
early_galaxies_bright_jwst.summary: New calculations show Lyα pressure can eject diffuse gas around dense clusters at Cosmic Dawn, making them visible while leaving star formation largely unaffected.
highlights: Lyα radiation pressure cannot overcome gravity in the densest filaments but efficiently clears low‑density gas and dust
The effect creates high‑speed winds that enhance the escape of ionizing photons from early galaxies
Researchers used post‑processed snapshots from radiation‑hydrodynamic simulations with the COLT Monte Carlo code
Findings explain why JWST observes unusually bright, compact star clusters only ~460 million years after the Big Bang

talin_mechanosensing_2026.institution: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS)
talin_mechanosensing_2026.headline: New Talin Mechanism Reveals Force‑Driven Self‑assembly in Cell Adhesions
talin_mechanosensing_2026.summary: Researchers discovered that mechanical force exposes talin’s aggregation‑prone region, prompting talin molecules to bind together and strengthen adhesion complexes.
highlights: Force unfolds talin, revealing the hidden APR that drives talin‑talin binding.
Vinculin acts as a mechano‑chaperone, disassembling force‑induced talin clusters.
The mechanism was shown using TIRF microscopy and biochemical assays in a PNAS 2026 study.

2611_07546v1.headline: Cold Collapse of Clustered Stars May Seed Massive Black Holes in Early Universe
2611_07546v1.summary: New theoretical work shows that rapid cold collapse of dense star clusters can trigger core collapse, potentially forming massive black holes shortly after the Big Bang.
highlights: James Webb Space Telescope observations reveal massive stellar systems at high redshift via gravitational lensing
Hierarchical systems of bound star clusters experience a faster 2‑body relaxation driven by stars per cluster
Cold collapse enhances mass segregation, allowing massive stars to dynamically decouple and undergo core collapse
Mergers increase cluster radii, but the most promising black‑hole pathway requires few or no mergers

survey_of_surveys_data_release_3_homogen.headline: Homogenised Stellar Parameters Unite Nine Spectroscopic Surveys
survey_of_surveys_data_release_3_homogen.summary: A new catalogue aligns temperatures, gravities and metallicities for over ten million Milky Way stars onto a common, validated scale.
highlights: Machine‑learning regression reduces APOGEE‑GALAH temperature offset from 44.5 K to 6.2 K
High‑quality subset shows median residuals of 30 K in Tₑff, 0.03 dex in log g, and –0.02 dex in [Fe/H]
Catalogue includes 10.13 million stars, with 6.10 million in a recommended high‑quality subset

cosmicgrain_dust_physics_module.headline: CosmicGrain Module Enables On‑the‑Fly Dust Physics in Galaxy Simulations
cosmicgrain_dust_physics_module.summary: CosmicGrain, built on Gadget-4, simulates active dust superparticles with drag, radiation pressure and subgrid processes, matching Milky Way dust profiles.
highlights: Dust superparticles experience resolved gas‑dust drag and radiation pressure, boosting ISM dust by ~100×.
Subgrid treatments include grain growth, thermal sputtering, coagulation, shattering, supernova shock destruction, and astration.
An eleven‑rung physics ladder (S0‑S10) at 1024³ resolution isolates each process’s impact on a Milky Way‑mass halo.
Silicate grains show a strongly asymmetric shattering destruction ratio, while carbon dust preferentially enriches the CGM.

2611_07524v1.headline: DESI Spectroscopy Confirms 71 New High‑Redshift Strong Lenses
2611_07524v1.summary: Using DESI spectra, researchers validated 71 of 80 HSC‑identified galaxy‑scale lenses at z > 0.8, nearly tripling known strong lenses in this epoch.
highlights: 71 systems show clear lensing features reproduced by lens models
Eight additional candidates are classified as probable or possible lenses
The sample expands high‑redshift strong‑lens catalog by almost three‑fold

cosmic_ray_populations_in_star_forming_a.headline: Fermi‑LAT Reveals Lower Cosmic‑Ray Electron Contribution in Starburst Galaxies
cosmic_ray_populations_in_star_forming_a.summary: A 15‑year Fermi‑LAT analysis shows M82 and NGC 253 emit less low‑energy gamma‑rays, indicating electron‑to‑proton ratios similar to the Milky Way.
highlights: Gamma‑ray spectra of M82 and NGC 253 drop below a few hundred MeV
Electron‑to‑proton ratios match Milky Way values, contrary to earlier estimates
Cosmic‑ray energy densities are 2.5–8 times below magnetic‑field energy in these starbursts
M31’s gamma‑ray emission splits into a soft central source and compact component
All studied starburst galaxies fall at or below the calorimetric limit

2611_07574v1.headline: Weak Lensing Sets Tight Limits on Supermassive Primordial Black Holes
2611_07574v1.summary: Analysis of DES Y3 weak‑lensing data constrains the fraction of supermassive primordial black holes, ruling out f_PBH ≈ 10⁻⁴ for masses above 10¹⁰ M☉.
highlights: DES Year 3 weak‑lensing measurements provide competitive constraints on supermassive PBHs
Case 1 accretion model excludes f_PBH ≳ 10⁻⁴ for M_PBH ≳ 10¹⁰ M☉
Forecasts for LSST suggest limits could improve by two orders of magnitude
Study distinguishes the seed effect from the Poisson effect in structure formation

electron_pairing_room_temp_sc.institution: Utrecht University, Leiden University, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich
electron_pairing_room_temp_sc.headline: Electron Pairing Alone Insufficient for Room‑Temperature Superconductivity
electron_pairing_room_temp_sc.summary: New study shows that while Cooper pairs form at high temperatures, achieving phase coherence remains the bottleneck for room‑temperature superconductivity.
highlights: Cooper pairs persist up to room temperature in cuprate samples
Phase coherence, not pairing, limits the onset of superconductivity
Research led by Utrecht University, Leiden University and Munich collaborators
Findings published in Science (2026) with DOI 10.1126/science.adt3444

dinosaur_blood_115myr.headline: Ancient Dinosaur Blood Molecules Survive 115 Million Years in Brazilian Fossil
dinosaur_blood_115myr.summary: Chemically confirmed heme and collagen amino acids were found in 115‑million‑year‑old Aratasaurus bones, overturning limits on biomolecule preservation.
highlights: Fossilized red blood cells containing heme were identified in vascular canals of Aratasaurus museunacionali.
Mineral hausmannite acted as a natural time‑capsule preserving blood molecules for 115 million years.
Study published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences with an international team from Curtin University, J‑AMST
Findings suggest new strategies for detecting ancient life on Earth and potentially on other planets.

jwst_glare_removal_hidden_planet.institution: James Webb Space Telescope team / machine‑learning collaborators
jwst_glare_removal_hidden_planet.headline: New AI‑Free Technique Reveals Hidden Exoplanet Around 51 Eridani
jwst_glare_removal_hidden_planet.summary: Scientists used a physics‑based digital twin and machine learning to strip JWST glare, uncovering the giant planet 51 Eridani b previously hidden in data.
highlights: Developed FLIP, a Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets method.
Created a digital twin of JWST to model detector optics without movement errors.
Applied the technique to JWST observations of 51 Eridani, revealing 51 Eridani b.
Approach promises to detect smaller, solar‑system‑like exoplanets beyond current limits.

valles_marineris_tectonic_activity.headline: Mars’ Valles Marineris Fault Still Active, Study Shows
valles_marineris_tectonic_activity.summary: Reanalysis of the 2021 S0976a marsquake reveals a slip‑strike event deep beneath Valles Marineris, proving the canyon’s faults remain tectonically active.
highlights: S0976a registered magnitude 4.2, the second‑largest marsquake recorded by NASA’s InSight lander.
The quake originated 20–40 km below the western side of Valles Marineris along a hidden fault line.
Researchers ruled out impacts and landslides, confirming tectonic slip as the cause.
Findings were published in Nature Communications by a team from Imperial College London.

ice_giants_magnetic_conductivity.institution: University of ... (research team analyzing Voyager 2 data)
ice_giants_magnetic_conductivity.headline: Deep Conductivity Shifts May Explain Ice Giants' Wacky Magnetic Fields
ice_giants_magnetic_conductivity.summary: New simulations suggest that increasing electrical conductivity deep inside Uranus and Neptune could cause their magnetic dipoles to tilt dramatically over decades.
highlights: Uranus' magnetic dipole tilt is 59° and Neptune's is 47°, far steeper than Earth's 11°
Computer models show conductivity increases with depth can drive dipole swings of tens of degrees in just decades
JWST infrared auroral images are being analyzed to track possible recent changes in the planets' magnetic fields

metamaterial_bone_tendon.headline: Delft Metamaterial Bridges Stiff Bone and Flexible Tendon Interfaces
metamaterial_bone_tendon.summary: Researchers at Delft University of Technology created a 3D‑printed metamaterial that smoothly transitions between stiff bone‑like lattices and compliant tendon‑like structures, enhancing implant durability.
highlights: Computational design identifies compatible geometries and inserts twinned unit cells to form a gradual transition zone
Printed hybrid lattices showed robust fatigue behavior and no unintended voids in µCT scans
The approach combines strut‑based lattices with triply periodic minimal surface sheets, optimizing stiffness and flexibility

quantum_gas_microscope_three_component_h.institution: International team (Germany, Thailand, India, China, United States)
quantum_gas_microscope_three_component_h.headline: Quantum Gas Microscope Captures First Tunable Three‑Component Hubbard System
quantum_gas_microscope_three_component_h.summary: An international team used a quantum gas microscope to image individual atoms in a tunable three‑component Hubbard lattice, opening new routes for quantum simulations.
highlights: Three distinct fermionic flavors were realized with independently tunable interactions.
The quantum gas microscope achieved single‑atom resolution of the lattice sites.
A Mott insulator state was observed despite potential three‑body loss.
Both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic correlations appeared within the same system.

vibrating_mirrors_black_hole_analog.headline: Ultracold Atom Cavity Mimics Black Hole Event Horizon
vibrating_mirrors_black_hole_analog.summary: Researchers at UC Santa Barbara demonstrated that vibrating light mirrors compress ultracold lithium atoms into pulses that emulate the one‑way flow of a black‑hole horizon.
highlights: Vibrating one of two laser‑sheet mirrors at ~100 Hz concentrates a diffuse cloud of lithium atoms into a tight packet
The matter‑wave Fabry‑Pérot cavity reproduces the one‑way flow predicted for light near black‑hole and white‑hole event horizons
Doubling the driving frequency creates two independent atom packets following distinct stable paths
Observed deviations from the ideal light‑like behavior arise from the atoms’ sub‑luminal speed variations

mega_heatwaves_interaction_study.institution: Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research & IIASA
mega_heatwaves_interaction_study.headline: Mega Heat Waves Amplified by Soil Moisture, Pressure and Temperature Feedbacks
mega_heatwaves_interaction_study.summary: A study led by PIK and IIASA shows a self‑reinforcing interaction that makes extreme heat waves up to 10% hotter as climate warms.
highlights: Machine‑learning analysis reveals a three‑way feedback among temperature, drying soils and high‑pressure systems.
In Central Europe the triggering threshold (~4 K above average, ≈29 °C) was crossed 23% of the time in 2018‑2022 versus 6% in
The feedback adds roughly 10% extra warming to the most severe mid‑latitude heat waves.
Current climate models underrepresent this mechanism, potentially underestimating future heat‑wave risk.

jwst_exoplanet_imaging_2026.headline: JWST Reveals Hidden Giant Exoplanet Using New Digital Twin Technique
jwst_exoplanet_imaging_2026.summary: A physics‑based learning algorithm called FLIP removed stellar glare from JWST data, exposing the 11‑Jupiter‑mass planet 51 Eridani b.
highlights: FLIP outperformed traditional processing by a factor of two to fifteen in tests on known exoplanet systems
The digital twin models millions of mirror imperfections and cryocooler‑induced vibrations
The technique recovered 51 Eridani b from observations taken two years earlier

future_warming_events_nature_comm.headline: Future Heatwaves Set to Exceed Recent Extreme Events, Study Shows
future_warming_events_nature_comm.summary: A Nature Communications study predicts future heatwaves will last longer, cover larger areas, and reach higher temperatures than any recorded since 2010.
highlights: Analysis of 22 heatwaves from 2010‑2023 across Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Americas
Model ensembles (CMIP5, CMIP6) project at least one exceptional heatwave per year in many regions by 2060‑2099
Future events could persist for months and affect a majority of Europe under high‑emission scenarios

microplastics_air_uas_method.headline: Uncrewed Aerial System Detects Microplastics 100 m Above Colorado
microplastics_air_uas_method.summary: A new CIRES-led method using a drone-mounted environmental cyclone sampler found microplastic particles up to 100 m altitude near highways and landfills.
highlights: Microplastics were sampled at 100 m (328 ft) above a heavily trafficked highway in Erie, Colorado.
The UAS flight time was limited to about 25 minutes, requiring large‑volume air sampling to capture enough particles.
Samples showed predominance of hetero‑aggregates, indicating mixed plastic and environmental material.
The proof‑of‑concept study demonstrates feasibility for atmospheric microplastic monitoring in remote or oceanic regions.

uv_metasurface_mirrors_2026.headline: University of Stuttgart engineers flat silicon metasurface that focuses 325 nm ultraviolet light
uv_metasurface_mirrors_2026.summary: Researchers etched elliptical air cavities into silicon, creating a flat metasurface that reflects and focuses 325 nm UV light with micrometer‑scale spots.
highlights: Elliptical air voids of ~470 nm length and 100 nm depth generate a geometric phase that redirects and focuses UV light
The metasurface focuses 325 nm light to ~1 µm spots with focal lengths from 5 mm to 1.25 mm and NA 0.15
Fabrication requires a single lithography‑etch step on standard silicon wafers, preserving mechanical robustness

north_cascades_magma_surge_timeline.headline: High‑precision dating pinpoints ancient magma surge in North Cascades
north_cascades_magma_surge_timeline.summary: Researchers used ultra‑precise uranium‑lead zircon dating to map a 79‑to‑60 million‑year magma flare‑up, revealing crustal thickening lagged behind magma influx.
highlights: The flare‑up spanned 79–60 million years ago along a Cretaceous continental arc in Washington.
Chemical abrasion–isotope dilution–thermal ionization mass spectrometry achieved age uncertainties as low as 0.05%.
Geochemical proxies show crustal thickening began only after the magma surge started.

crystal_structure_breakthrough.headline: MIT Researchers Use Floppy Polymers to Forge Unseen Nanoparticle Crystals
crystal_structure_breakthrough.summary: By replacing rigid ligands with flexible PEG chains, MIT scientists directed gold nanoparticle assembly into crystal structures never observed before.
highlights: Flexible PEG ligands allow precise control of bond numbers between gold nanoparticles
Ordered crystal lattices formed without pre‑designing particle connections
Approach overturns a 20‑year rule that rigid ligands are required for assembly

record_low_temp_space.institution: Chinese Academy of Sciences (Tiangong Space Station)
record_low_temp_space.headline: Tiangong Space Station Sets Record 10 pK Temperature for Quantum Experiments
record_low_temp_space.summary: Researchers on China’s Tiangong station cooled 20,000 rubidium atoms to 9.7 picokelvin, the coldest environment ever achieved in space, enabling new quantum studies.
highlights: Achieved equivalent temperature of 9.7 pK, four times lower than the previous 38 pK record.
Measured atom cloud expansion for 7 seconds, far longer than prior space experiments.
Utilized optical dipole traps with laser cooling and evaporative cooling on ~20,000 rubidium atoms.
Opens path for space‑based atom interferometers and studies of exotic quantum phases.

ai_mitochondrial_protein_targets.headline: AI uncovers hidden mitochondrial protein interactions, revealing new disease targets
ai_mitochondrial_protein_targets.summary: Using AlphaFold‑Multimer, Texas A&M researchers mapped 2,895 likely mitochondrial protein pairs, linking unknown proteins to disease pathways and offering therapeutic clues.
highlights: Screened ~630,000 possible pairings of ~1,100 human mitochondrial proteins
Identified 2,895 probable interactions, over half previously unreported
Provided first probable partners for 85 uncharacterized proteins
Created free online resource MitoMatch for global research use

boron_oxygen_breakthrough.headline: Würzburg Chemists Isolate Stable Oxoboranes After 60‑Year Quest
boron_oxygen_breakthrough.summary: A team led by Holger Braunschweig at University of Würzburg has unexpectedly synthesized and isolated stable oxoboranes, solving a six‑decade chemistry puzzle.
highlights: Oxoboranes, previously thought too unstable, were produced from simple diboracumulene‑ketone reactions
Three distinct oxoborane compounds were isolated, demonstrating the method’s versatility
Computational support from Ashwini K. Phukan’s group at Tezpur University confirmed the structures
The work appears in the peer‑reviewed journal Nature Chemistry (2026)

aav_tumor_risk.headline: AAV Gene Therapy Linked to Tumor Development in New Cases
aav_tumor_risk.summary: Recent case series provides definitive evidence that adeno-associated viruses can trigger tumor formation, reshaping risk assessments for gene‑therapy patients.
highlights: Multiple tumor cases documented in 2024‑2025 are linked to AAV vectors
The study settles a two‑decade debate about AAV oncogenic potential
Implications for spinal muscular atrophy treatments at University of Rochester
Researchers urge revised safety protocols for future gene therapies

ai_driven_solid_electrolyte_discovery_fr.headline: AI‑Driven Framework Targets Fast, Stable Solid Electrolytes for Safer Batteries
ai_driven_solid_electrolyte_discovery_fr.summary: A new AI‑integrated loop links databases, simulations, LLMs and autonomous experiments to accelerate discovery of reliable solid electrolytes for batteries.
highlights: Living materials databases capture synthesis and testing data for solid electrolytes.
AI‑powered interatomic potentials simulate ion transport over realistic timescales.
Large language models extract hidden knowledge from literature to guide candidate selection.
Autonomous experiments rapidly validate AI‑suggested materials, feeding results back into the loop.

climate_dengue_himalayas.headline: Dengue Fever Ascends Himalayas as Climate Warms Nepal’s High Altitudes
climate_dengue_himalayas.summary: Rising temperatures in Nepal’s mountains have enabled Aedes mosquitoes to colonize elevations up to 2,500 m, sparking dengue outbreaks across most districts.
highlights: Aedes aegypti now found at 2,500 m, previously limited to lowland Terai
2025 saw ~9,000 dengue cases and six deaths in Nepal, affecting 76 of 77 districts
Rapid urban water storage and flash‑flood‑induced standing water create ideal breeding sites for both Aedes aegypti and Aedes
Researchers link the mosquito expansion to higher minimum temperatures and unplanned urbanization, as documented in a

cmb_patterns_2026.headline: South Pole Telescopes Probe B‑Mode Polarization to Test Cosmic Inflation
cmb_patterns_2026.summary: Combining data from the South Pole Telescope and BICEP arrays, researchers aim to detect B‑mode signals that could confirm primordial gravitational waves from inflation.
highlights: The SPT and BICEP instruments operate in Antarctica’s radio‑quiet zone to measure millimeter‑scale CMB wavelengths.
Detecting B‑mode polarization would provide direct evidence of primordial gravitational waves generated during inflation.
The effort builds on the 2002 polarization detection by the Degree Angular Scale Interferometer and subsequent upgrades.

rubin_hidden_companions_2026.headline: Rubin Observatory Uncovers Two Ultra‑Faint Milky Way Companions
rubin_hidden_companions_2026.summary: Using only 7% of its preview data, the Vera C.
highlights: Aquarius IV lies about 355,000 light‑years from Earth and is one of the faintest known dwarf galaxies
Rubin‑GC1 is a star cluster concealed behind thick cosmic dust on the opposite side of the Milky Way
The discoveries were made with the 8.4‑meter Simonyi Survey Telescope and its 3.2‑gigapixel camera

quantum_simulation_lattice_gauge.headline: Hybrid Trapped Ions Reveal Aharonov‑Bohm Interference in Z₂ Lattice Gauge Simulation
quantum_simulation_lattice_gauge.summary: Using two strontium ions, researchers at University of Oxford demonstrated flux‑dependent tunneling, confirming the Aharonov‑Bohm effect in a synthetic Z₂ lattice gauge loop.
highlights: Two electronic qubits encoded gauge fields while ion vibrations stored matter particles.
Entangling the qubits created zero‑flux or vison states, altering interference.
Zero‑flux configuration doubled tunneling speed; vison flux completely suppressed particle motion.
Results match numerical simulations including decoherence and open path to larger synthetic lattices.

polar_vortex_faltering_weeks_earlier_tha.headline: Polar Vortex Disrupts in Early November, Setting Record Earliest Breakup
polar_vortex_faltering_weeks_earlier_tha.summary: For the first time since records began, the stratospheric polar vortex began weakening in early November, driven by strong El Niño‑amplified Rossby waves and a high‑pressure anomaly.
highlights: ECMWF scientists Tim Stockdale and Frederic Vitart identified the earliest observed stratospheric vortex disruption.
MIT climatologist Judah Cohen linked the surge of tropospheric Rossby waves to a sudden stratospheric warming forecast by Nov 20.
France’s Meteo‑France and Britain’s Met Office warn the event could trigger cold air outbreaks across the U.S., Europe and East
Only three November sudden stratospheric warmings have been recorded since the 1950s (1958, 1968, 2025).

ancient_forest_europe.headline: Europe's Ancient Landscapes Were Open Woodlands, Not Dense Forests, Study Finds
ancient_forest_europe.summary: A 20‑million‑year paleoecological analysis shows Europe was dominated by mixed woodlands, grasslands and grazing megafauna, challenging modern reforestation goals.
highlights: Evidence from fossil pollen, charcoal, and ancient eDNA reveals a shifting mosaic of trees and open habitats over 20 million
Large herbivores such as elephants, rhinos and bison maintained openness by grazing and trampling vegetation.
The study, published in Biological Conservation, argues that dense‑forest planting may harm biodiversity adapted to historic

dead_star_double_ring.headline: Double Debris Discs Around White Dwarf Hint at Sun’s Distant Fate
dead_star_double_ring.summary: Astronomers using ESO’s VLT discovered two chemically distinct rings of planetary wreckage around white dwarf J1328‑1450, suggesting surviving Pluto‑sized bodies may shape them.
highlights: The double-ring system was observed with the X‑Shooter spectrograph on the VLT in Chile.
Inner and outer rings show different magnesium abundances, implying origins from separate destroyed planets.
Gravitational influence of two unseen planetesimals, one possibly as large as Pluto or the Moon, likely maintains the gap.
The findings offer a rare preview of how our Solar System may appear billions of years after the Sun becomes a white dwarf.
