human_bodies_produce_2_billion_metric_to.headline: Human Metabolism Emits 2 Billion Tonnes of CO₂ Annually, Study Finds
human_bodies_produce_2_billion_metric_to.summary: A University of Bath modelling study shows human metabolic CO₂ output rose 74% from 1985 to 2015, reaching 2.05 billion metric tons.
highlights: Human metabolic CO₂ production increased from 1.18 billion to 2.05 billion metric tons between 1985 and 2015.
Population growth accounts for over 60% of the rise, with per‑person emissions changing little.
The research, published in The Lancet Planetary Health, differentiates biological CO₂ from fossil‑fuel emissions.
Accurate metabolic CO₂ estimates can refine global carbon‑cycle models and improve climate‑policy forecasts.

mars_stinky_gas_volcanism.headline: Hydrogen Chloride Detected Over Alba Mons Suggests Ongoing Martian Volcanism
mars_stinky_gas_volcanism.summary: ESA’s ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter identified trace hydrogen chloride emissions near Alba Mons, indicating possible active magmatic processes beneath Mars’ surface.
highlights: HCl was measured in parts‑per‑billion concentrations above fissured terrain on the northern Tharsis Plateau.
Detections peak during early northern summer when the atmosphere is clear and ice sublimates, favoring magmatic release.
The study, published in Science Advances, proposes deep volcanic or mud‑volcano origins over atmospheric explanations.
Co‑lead author Daniel Mège of the Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences called the signal the “smoking gun” of

euclid_galaxy_catalog.headline: Euclid Maps 26 Million Galaxies, Reveals Deep Fields Up to 10.5 Billion Light‑Years
euclid_galaxy_catalog.summary: In its first week, ESA’s Euclid mission identified 26 million galaxies across 63 sq deg, with the most distant reaching 10.5 billion light‑years.
highlights: 26 million galaxies detected in a single week of scanning
Three deep‑field regions cover 63 square degrees, equivalent to over 300 full Moons
Farthest galaxies observed lie 10.5 billion light‑years away
Mission will revisit these fields tens of times before the 2030 nominal end

functional_organization_occipitotemporal.headline: Refined Animacy‑Size Maps Reveal No Single Dominant Principle in Occipitotemporal Cortex
functional_organization_occipitotemporal.summary: Using the THINGS‑fMRI dataset, researchers show that animacy and size organize visual cortex but are not uniquely dominant over other object properties.
highlights: Animacy gradients replicated across three participants, aligning with fusiform face area and occipital place area preferences
Real‑world size maps displayed asymmetric partitions, including unexpected large‑object responses in fusiform face area
Analysis of 15 object properties found multiple smooth topographies, with none emerging as clearly dominant

euclid_deep_dive_universe.headline: Euclid Maps 26 Million Galaxies in First Deep‑Field Survey
euclid_deep_dive_universe.summary: In just one week Euclid observed 26 million galaxies across 63 sq deg, spotting objects up to 10.5 billion light‑years distant.
highlights: Euclid scanned three sky regions covering 63 square degrees, equivalent to over 300 full Moons.
The survey detected 26 million galaxies, with the most distant at 10.5 billion light‑years.
By 2030 the mission will revisit these fields tens of times, ultimately mapping one‑third of the sky (14 000 square degrees).

stera_constellation_agreement.headline: ESA and Eumetsat Seal Deal for EPS‑Sterna Constellation Launch by 2029
stera_constellation_agreement.summary: The new agreement will fund a fleet of Sterna satellites, building on the Arctic Weather Satellite’s success, to improve short‑term forecasts worldwide.
highlights: EPS‑Sterna will provide frequent Arctic observations for very short‑term weather nowcasts.
First Sterna satellite targeted for launch in 2029 after ESA’s procurement management.
The constellation follows ESA’s Arctic Weather Satellite, operational since August 2024.
Collaboration mirrors ESA’s Meteosat and MetOp meteorological programmes.
Agreement signed by ESA Director Simonetta Cheli and Eumetsat DG Phil Evans at the European Space Conference in Brussels.

record_breaking_xray_power.headline: Record‑Breaking 300‑Attosecond X‑Ray Flash Focused to Nanometre Spot
record_breaking_xray_power.summary: Scientists at European XFEL generated 300‑attosecond hard‑X‑ray pulses concentrated into a 180 × 330 nm spot, achieving intensity above 10²⁰ W cm⁻².
highlights: Each pulse lasted only 300 attoseconds, a billionth of a billionth of a second.
The advanced Kirkpatrick‑Baez (AKB) mirror system focused the beam to a 180 × 330 nm focal area.
Peak intensity exceeded 10²⁰ watts per square centimetre, confirmed by amplified spontaneous emission in copper.
The results were published in Optica and represent a world record in hard‑X‑ray attosecond fluence and intensity.

tectonic_plate_tears_iran.headline: Two Giant Tears Found Beneath Iran’s Arabian Plate
tectonic_plate_tears_iran.summary: Researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences identified two massive slab tears in the Arabian Plate beneath southeastern Iran, revealing a rare snapshot of tectonic transition.
highlights: Seismic data from 69 stations (Mar 2017‑Sep 2018) show a horizontal tear at the Zagros‑Makran junction and a smaller vertical
Oceanic slab subducted to depths ≥450 km while continental lithosphere only reached ≤300 km, creating contrasting tearing modes
Models suggest the two tears could merge over several million years, potentially influencing regional magmatism

mars_gas_leaks_volcanic_activity.headline: Hydrogen Chloride Leaks Hint Mars May Still Host Active Volcanoes
mars_gas_leaks_volcanic_activity.summary: Unusual hydrogen chloride emissions above fresh fractures in the Alba Mons region suggest that deep‑seated magma could still be venting on present‑day Mars.
highlights: ESA’s ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter detected elevated HCl concentrations during early northern summer
CaSSIS images revealed narrow, fresh fractures extending hundreds of metres on Alba Mons
Team led by Alexander Trokhimovskiy proposes a dormant magma chamber feeding the gas leaks
Findings published in Science Advances (2026) argue Mars retains enough internal heat for intermittent volcanism

nuclear_asteroid_deflection.headline: Nuclear X‑ray Blast Could Deflect Asteroid, But Aim Is Critical
nuclear_asteroid_deflection.summary: Show that directing a nuclear X‑ray burst at the right side of an irregular asteroid can boost deflection speed up to fivefold, while a wrong aim may fail.
highlights: Deflection velocity varied from 3.9 mm/s to 0.8 mm/s depending on blast direction, a fivefold difference.
Rotation change differed by a factor of 17 for the same asteroid when hit from opposite sides.
The new model combines ALEGRA and SPARTA codes, running 1,600 times faster than previous simulations.
Research published in Icarus (2026) was funded by Sandia’s Laboratory Directed Research and Development program.

new_tnos_27.headline: 27 New Trans‑Neptunian Objects Reveal Pristine Planetary Building Blocks
new_tnos_27.summary: Astronomers using Hubble and James Webb observed 27 tiny TNOs, finding their colours unchanged and challenging planet‑formation models.
highlights: The objects are as small as 5 km across, making them the faintest directly observed TNOs.
Their surface colours match those of much larger TNOs, indicating little alteration since formation.
Fewer tiny TNOs were detected than predicted by several planet‑formation simulations.

primordial_black_holes_dark_matter.headline: Stupendously Large Primordial Black Holes Excluded as Dark Matter Candidates
primordial_black_holes_dark_matter.summary: New calculations show that even immensely massive primordial black holes cannot constitute a significant fraction of the universe’s dark matter, according to CMB constraints.
highlights: Nicholas Leister’s team at Mainz Institute for Theoretical Physics modeled random PBH distributions and derived expected
Comparison with cosmic microwave background measurements rules out PBHs ≥ 100 billion M☉ contributing more than a negligible
The analysis also challenges PBH‑seeded formation scenarios for early massive galaxies observed by James Webb Space Telescope.

rubin_retrograde_object_neptune.headline: Rubin Observatory Discovers Retrograde Object Beyond Neptune
rubin_retrograde_object_neptune.summary: A newly identified body, designated R631, follows a 142‑degree retrograde orbit at 32 AU, hinting at a possible cometary origin beyond Neptune.
highlights: Orbital inclination of 142° places R631 on a highly tilted, opposite‑direction path.
Located 32 AU from the Sun, it will reach perihelion at 24 AU in October 2047.
Estimated diameter ~100 km, comparable to comet Bernardinelli–Bernstein.
Origin theories include capture from another system or scattering by Neptune within the Kuiper belt.

room_temp_exotic_state.headline: Room‑Temperature Supersolid Observed in Exciton‑Polariton Bose‑Einstein Condensate
room_temp_exotic_state.summary: An international team created a room‑temperature supersolid exciton‑polariton Bose‑Einstein condensate using a voltage‑controlled liquid‑crystal microcavity that operates up to 60 °C.
highlights: The supersolid formed at temperatures up to 60 °C, eliminating the need for cryogenic cooling.
Created in a microcavity combining liquid crystal and organic semiconductor, driven by laser pulses.
Observed spontaneous symmetry breaking with stripe patterns shifting each laser pulse, matching theoretical predictions.
Experiments reproduced across multiple samples and supported by computer simulations.

arxiv_2611_08641v1.headline: ALMA Reveals Gas Flows Feeding Forming High‑Mass Binary in NGC 6334I(N)
arxiv_2611_08641v1.summary: High‑resolution ALMA imaging shows ordered circumbinary motion and multiple inflows delivering material to the nascent 5 M⊙ primary and 2 M⊙ secondary in NGC 6334I(N).
highlights: Cold CH₃OH lines trace a ~1000 au circumbinary rotation around the 740 au‑separated protostars.
The secondary’s mass is estimated at 2 M⊙, while the primary is about 5 M⊙.
Inflow rates of ~10⁻⁶–10⁻⁴ M⊙ yr⁻¹ are identified feeding the circumstellar disks.

arxiv_2611_08585v1.headline: New Study Shows CMB Features Distinguish Primordial From Post‑Inflationary Signals
arxiv_2611_08585v1.summary: Researchers use principal component analysis of the Cosmic Microwave Background to show that scale‑dependent patterns can reveal whether new physics originated before or after inflation.
highlights: Primordial "sharp" and "resonant" features produce oscillatory signatures with arbitrary frequency and running
Exotic energy injection and early dark energy generate qualitatively different CMB patterns
Principal component analysis finds no significant degeneracy between the two classes of signals

arxiv_2611_08742v1.headline: Gravity‑Boosted Neutrino Annihilation Near Black‑Hole Discs Reveals Flavour Geometry
arxiv_2611_08742v1.summary: A new fast moment method shows that general‑relativistic transport and neutrino flavour conversion interact differently depending on the spatial arrangement of neutrino emission zones.
highlights: Gravity enhances annihilation energy deposition by factors of 1.4–5 compared with flat space
Uniform flavour conversion alters conversion effects by ≤6% for most temperature profiles, keeping separability approximate
Relativistic bending of inner‑ring heavy‑lepton neutrinos can raise conversion factors up to 2.4 times flat‑space values
In a Kerr configuration, flavour equipartition reduces deposition by 54% in flat space but increases it by 11% in curved spacetime

primordial_non_gaussianity_large_scale_c.headline: New Cosmic‑Web Bias Method Reveals Primordial Non‑Gaussianity Signals
primordial_non_gaussianity_large_scale_c.summary: Researchers reformulate the large‑scale $k^{-2}$ bias from local‑type primordial non‑Gaussianity as an anisotropic environmental effect using a Hessian field.
highlights: Define a Hessian field \(\mathcal{H}_{ij}\) whose trace reproduces the $k^{-2}$ enhancement of the Dalal et al. bias term.
Diagonalize \(\mathcal{H}_{ij}\) to identify four large‑scale web environments analogous to knots, filaments, sheets and voids.
Tested with the AbacusPNG suite of local‑PNG N‑body simulations for $f_{\rm NL}=\{-100,-30,30,100\}$ and recover the expected
Show that existing halo catalogs can be post‑processed to imprint an effective $f_{\rm NL}$ signature without new simulations.

arxiv_2611_08642v1.headline: PHANTOM SPH Simulations Reveal Tidal Imprint on Neutron Star Gravitational Waves
arxiv_2611_08642v1.summary: Using the Newtonian SPH code PHANTOM, researchers show that tidal effects in a 1.5 + 1.5 Msun binary neutron star can be extracted with about 10⁴ particles.
highlights: Tidal contribution matches waveforms calibrated against full numerical GR simulations.
Accurate tidal extraction requires ≥10⁴ smoothed particles for NS–NS binaries.
At separations >100 km tidal signal falls below SPH numerical noise, making point‑mass waveforms sufficient.
White dwarf–neutron star binaries need far more particles and larger separations, limiting the method’s usefulness.

ozempic_ckd.headline: Semaglutide Shows Promise in Reversing Chronic Kidney Disease Damage
ozempic_ckd.summary: A Nature Medicine study finds the weight‑loss drug semaglutide restores kidney blood vessels, improves filtration and reduces inflammation in chronic kidney disease patients.
highlights: Semaglutide increased kidney blood flow and reduced vessel stiffness in a 106‑participant subset.
Urinary albumin levels fell, indicating tighter filtration barriers.
Metabolic‑stress and inflammatory genes were down‑regulated while repair genes were up‑regulated in glomeruli.
Prior NEJM trial showed semaglutide cut risk of kidney failure, heart attack and stroke, leading to early termination.

cern_rare_decay_2026.headline: CERN's LHCb Finds Evidence of Ultra‑Rare Bd → μ⁺μ⁻ Decay
cern_rare_decay_2026.summary: After four decades, CERN scientists observed evidence for the Bd → μ⁺μ⁻ decay, a process expected only once in about ten billion beauty particle decays.
highlights: The LHCb upgrade in 2024 increased data collection fivefold, enabling the rare signal detection.
Combined 2024‑2025 data with earlier runs yields a significance of 3.2 σ, surpassing the evidence threshold.
The measured rate matches Standard Model predictions, tightening constraints on new physics.
Future High Luminosity LHC upgrades aim to reach five‑sigma observation by increasing dataset size tenfold.

mars_volcanism_hcl_detection.headline: Enigmatic HCl Detections Hint at Ongoing Magma Chambers Beneath Alba Mons
mars_volcanism_hcl_detection.summary: New Science Advances study finds hydrogen chloride near Alba Mons during aphelion, suggesting active magma chambers on a planet once thought volcanically dead.
highlights: Aphelion HCl detections are localized over Alba Mons, unlike seasonal perihelion signals
Fresh sub‑meter fissures identified by HiRISE may act as pathways from deep magmatic bodies
Seepage calculations rule out atmospheric aerosol origins for the aphelion HCl
The findings build on InSight marsquake data and ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter observations

methane_microbes_nanowires_2026.headline: Methane‑Eating ANME Build Conductive Nanowires on Electrodes
methane_microbes_nanowires_2026.summary: Researchers at Radboud University have cultured anaerobic methanotrophic archaea that grow on electrodes, produce conductive nanowires, and convert methane into measurable electric current.
highlights: ANME attach to a low‑voltage electrode and divide every five days, far faster than in natural habitats
The microbes generate a small but steady electric current by transmitting electrons through OmcZ‑type cytochrome nanowires
Cultures achieved ~95% purity of ANME, the highest reported for this group
Potential applications include more efficient hydrogen production than conventional electrolyzers, though commercial use remains

stroke_drug_approval.headline: FDA Approves Bayer’s Sunharbo to Cut Stroke Recurrence Risk
stroke_drug_approval.summary: The FDA cleared Bayer’s Sunharbo, a factor XIa inhibitor, after a Phase 3 trial showed a 26% reduction in recurrent strokes versus placebo.
highlights: In the Phase 3 trial, 8.4% of placebo patients suffered a secondary stroke compared with 6.2% on Sunharbo.
The drug targets protein XIa, aiming to prevent clot formation without raising bleeding risk.
Number needed to treat is 53 patients per year to prevent one recurrent stroke.

zfx_autism.headline: X‑chromosome gene ZFX may shield girls from autism
zfx_autism.summary: Researchers found that the X‑linked gene ZFX boosts expression of autism‑associated genes, potentially explaining the lower autism prevalence in females.
highlights: ZFX expression is higher in female brains and appears to buffer autism‑risk genes
CRISPR‑based RNA knockdown of 20 autism‑linked genes revealed strong convergence onto a core network of 70 genes
The study identified a central hub of 70 genes and highlighted ZFX as a key regulator in the female protective effect

axion_search_alpsii.headline: ALPS II Sets New Sensitivity Record in Lab Axion Search
axion_search_alpsii.summary: The ALPS II experiment at DESY reported its first campaign, finding no axion signal but achieving a sensitivity over twenty times greater than previous lab searches.
highlights: ALPS II uses 24 superconducting dipole magnets and dual optical cavities to boost photon‑axion conversion.
The February‑May 2024 run improved sensitivity by 12 orders of magnitude relative to early “light‑shining‑through‑a‑wall” tests.
No axion‑like particles were detected; stray light caused a background of two photons per hour.
The result is 20 × more sensitive than any prior laboratory axion search.

arctic_arsenic_traced_to_montana_mine.headline: Arsenic Traced to Montana’s Anaconda Mine in Arctic Ice Cores
arctic_arsenic_traced_to_montana_mine.summary: New Nature Sustainability study links early‑20th‑century arsenic spikes in Arctic ice to emissions from Montana’s Anaconda Copper Mine, revealing delayed pollution controls.
highlights: Arsenic levels peaked around 1914, fifteen times pre‑industrial values
Electrostatic precipitators installed after 1919 cut emissions by ~65%
Delayed controls added ~60,000 tons of arsenic and 24,000 tons of lead to the atmosphere
Modeling shows 55% of Americans and 11% of Canadians were exposed to elevated arsenic risk

xenon_core_hole_decay_2026.institution: Institute for Molecular Science (Japan) and partners
xenon_core_hole_decay_2026.headline: Synchrotron Pulse Pairs Capture Femtosecond Decay of Xenon Core Hole
xenon_core_hole_decay_2026.summary: Researchers used phase‑coherent extreme‑ultraviolet pulse pairs to directly observe the ~6‑fs Auger decay of a xenon 4d core hole in real time.
highlights: Phase‑coherent pulse pairs from the UVSOR‑III synchrotron produced 93.4 eV photons with attosecond‑level delay control
Interference fringe contrast decayed within a few femtoseconds, matching the known ~6 fs lifetime of the xenon 4d hole
A 2 fs oscillation in the contrast revealed coherent spin‑orbit splitting consistent with established values

alzheimer_outside_brain_signs_2026.headline: Alzheimer’s Mutations Disrupt Muscle Nerves, Hinting at Early Peripheral Warning Signs
alzheimer_outside_brain_signs_2026.summary: Using human‑on‑a‑chip neuromuscular models, UCF researchers showed that familial Alzheimer’s mutations impair nerve‑to‑muscle communication, suggesting movement deficits may appear before memory loss.
highlights: Familial Alzheimer’s mutations caused abnormal signaling at the neuromuscular junction in a brain‑free microphysiological system.
The study was funded by the NIH National Institute on Aging and published in Alzheimer’s & Dementia: The Journal of the
Human‑on‑a‑chip technology allowed direct observation of peripheral nerve pathology without animal models.
Researchers propose that gait and balance tests could serve as early biomarkers for Alzheimer’s.

bacteriophage_protein_inhibits_cell_wall.headline: Phage Protein Sgl PP7 Locks Bacterial MurJ, Halting Cell‑Wall Synthesis
bacteriophage_protein_inhibits_cell_wall.summary: Cryo‑EM structures show the phage lysis protein Sgl PP7 inserts its tail into MurJ, freezing it in an outward‑facing state and blocking lipid II transport.
highlights: Sgl PP7 binds MurJ’s lipid‑binding groove and plugs a deep cavity with its C‑terminal tail.
This interaction stabilizes MurJ in an outward‑facing conformation, preventing lipid II translocation.
Similar conformational locking is observed with other phage proteins Lys M and Sgl CJ3, indicating convergent evolution.
Cryo‑electron microscopy resolved the MurJ–Sgl PP7 complex at near‑atomic resolution.
Findings provide a structural template for designing new antibiotics targeting MurJ.

chlorine_anion_redox_battery_cathodes.headline: Chlorine Anion Redox Unveiled in Solid‑State Battery Cathode Li₂FeCl₄
chlorine_anion_redox_battery_cathodes.summary: Researchers demonstrate that chlorine atoms in Li₂FeCl₄ participate in high‑voltage oxidation, revealing a new anion redox mechanism for halide cathodes.
highlights: Electrochemical tests show two oxidation plateaus at ~3.8 V (Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺) and ~4.2 V (chlorine) in an all‑solid‑state cell
X‑ray photoelectron and absorption spectroscopy detect changes in chlorine’s electronic state during charging
Density functional theory identifies occupied chlorine‑derived nonbonding orbitals capable of charge compensation
Structural analysis reveals Fe–Cl octahedral distortion and partial iron reduction linked to chlorine redox

forbidden_vibrations_single_molecules.headline: Basel Team Controls Forbidden Vibrations in Single Molecules Using Quantum-Logic Spectroscopy
forbidden_vibrations_single_molecules.summary: Researchers at the University of Basel have repeatedly measured and coherently controlled forbidden vibrational transitions in single nitrogen molecular ions without destroying them.
highlights: Quantum-logic spectroscopy uses a calcium ion as a messenger to read the state of a nitrogen molecular ion.
The technique allowed identification of several forbidden vibrational lines and a ten‑fold improvement in frequency precision.
Repeated measurements on the same molecule made detection of billion‑times weaker transitions feasible.
The identified transitions are highly insensitive to external disturbances, promising for molecular clocks and qubits.

oldest_compact_quasar_pair.headline: Oldest Compact Quasar Pair Discovered at Cosmic Dawn
oldest_compact_quasar_pair.summary: Astronomers using Gemini North and JWST have identified Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, a pair of supermassive quasars only 900 million years after the Big Bang.
highlights: The quasars are separated by ~18,100 light‑years and have masses of 1.5 billion and 400 million M☉.
They were found in the JWST Aether survey, which sampled 200 quasars representing 43 % of known early‑Universe quasars.
Gemini North’s GNIRS and GMOS instruments resolved the faint companion despite its extreme distance.
Their existence challenges current models of supermassive black‑hole growth in the first billion years.

little_red_dots_black_hole_birthplaces.headline: James Webb 'little red dots' identified as birthplaces of early supermassive black holes
little_red_dots_black_hole_birthplaces.summary: Advanced simulations suggest the compact, bright sources seen by JWST are primordial galaxies harboring ~10 million‑solar‑mass black holes hidden within dense gas.
highlights: LRDs are compact (≈500 light‑years) galaxies containing ~100 million stars
Simulations reproduce the distinctive V‑shaped spectra observed by JWST
Black holes of ~10 million solar masses are enshrouded by dense gas, suppressing X‑ray emission
The model matches the full range of observed LRD properties across redshifts

first_direct_cosmic_hydrogen_measurement.headline: MeerKAT Achieves First Direct Map of Cosmic Hydrogen Across 4.5 Billion Years
first_direct_cosmic_hydrogen_measurement.summary: The MeerKLASS team used 21‑cm intensity mapping with MeerKAT to directly measure large‑scale cosmic hydrogen, confirming its alignment with the cosmic web.
highlights: First direct detection of neutral hydrogen signal from 4.5 billion years ago using ~250 deg² of MeerKAT data
Innovative observation mode treated each of the 64 dishes as independent telescopes, boosting survey speed
Results validate 21‑cm intensity mapping as a powerful cosmological tool for probing dark energy and dark matter
Study published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society after a decade‑long international effort

quantum_error_correction_complexity.headline: Memory Effects Challenge Quantum Error‑Correction Assumptions
quantum_error_correction_complexity.summary: New studies reveal long‑lived environmental defects cause non‑Markovian noise in superconducting qubits, complicating error‑correction strategies for scalable quantum computers.
highlights: Ioan Pop’s team detected very long‑lived spurious states in a superconducting qubit’s environment
Rami Barends observed similar Markov‑assumption violations in another superconducting qubit
Analyses of Google’s Willow and IBM cloud machines showed non‑Markovian models fit observed errors better
QLDPC codes are emerging but their performance against correlated noise remains untested

earth_core_carbon_origin.headline: Outer‑Solar‑System Meteorites Delivered Heavy Carbon to Earth’s Core
earth_core_carbon_origin.summary: A Yale‑Columbia analysis of Hawaiian melt inclusions shows carbon‑13‑rich core carbon matches outer‑solar‑system carbonaceous chondrites, arriving late in Earth’s formation.
highlights: Melt inclusions from historic Hawaiian eruptions reveal the isotopic signature of core carbon
Carbon‑13 enrichment indicates a source distinct from inner‑solar‑system material
The signature aligns precisely with carbon‑rich carbonaceous chondrite meteorites
Core carbon likely entered during the final stage of Earth’s main assembly

constraints_on_lorentz_invariance_violat.headline: LHAASO Detects PeV Gamma Rays from Cygnus X‑3, Tightening Lorentz Violation Limits
constraints_on_lorentz_invariance_violat.summary: The Large High‑Altitude Air Shower Observatory observed 3.7 PeV photons from Cygnus X‑3, allowing researchers to push Lorentz invariance violation limits to above 10⁻² Mₚₗ.
highlights: LHAASO recorded photons up to 3.7 PeV during a Cygnus X‑3 flare
Superluminal LIV would cause rapid photon decay, producing a spectral cutoff
No cutoff was seen, implying LIV effects are suppressed
Second‑order LIV energy scale is now constrained above 10⁻² Mₚₗ

2611_13733v1.headline: Scalar‑Induced Gravitational Waves Reveal Early‑Universe Phase Transitions
2611_13733v1.summary: Scalar‑induced gravitational waves can map the equation‑of‑state changes during early‑Universe phase transitions, offering new probes from PTA to space‑based detectors.
highlights: SIGWs encode the time‑dependent equation of state and sound speed of the cosmic thermal bath
A step in the GW spectrum arises from entropy dilution for a scale‑invariant curvature spectrum
The QCD crossover produces a signal around 10 nHz, detectable by NANOGrav 15‑year data
TeV‑scale BSM transitions generate mHz signals within reach of LISA, Taiji and TianQin

2611_13343v1.headline: TESS Finds Hot Jupiter TOI-2535 b Losing Its Transits
2611_13343v1.summary: Over seven years, TESS observed the hot Jupiter TOI-2535 b’s transit chord drift off its star, driven by a mutually inclined Saturn‑mass perturber.
highlights: Transit impact parameter changed at 0.16 yr⁻¹, moving the chord off the stellar disk
Transit mid‑times deviated up to 6 hours from a linear ephemeris
NEID radial‑velocity data reveal a nearby inclined planetary companion
Dynamical modeling suggests the perturber is at least Saturn‑mass in a mean‑motion resonance

ultra_high_energy_cosmic_rays_require_me.headline: Metal‑Rich Sources Needed to Explain Ultra‑High‑Energy Cosmic Rays
ultra_high_energy_cosmic_rays_require_me.summary: Analysis of Pierre Auger Observatory data shows that ultra‑high‑energy cosmic rays require source metallicities far exceeding those of typical low‑energy cosmic‑ray seeds.
highlights: Fits to Pierre Auger Observatory measurements above $10^{17.8}$ eV reveal two composition scenarios
Only the mixed primary‑secondary proton solution matches hydrogen abundances of low‑energy cosmic rays
Both scenarios demand an overabundance of silicon‑iron group nuclei at the source

cosmic_string_networks_with_time_varying.headline: Simulations Reveal Scaling of Time‑Varying Cosmic String Networks
cosmic_string_networks_with_time_varying.summary: Large‑scale field‑theory simulations show that cosmic strings with tension varying as a power of the scale factor follow VOS scaling during radiation and matter eras.
highlights: Modified Abelian‑Higgs model used with tension μ ∝ a^{-2m} for m = –0.5 to 0.5.
Simulations run on 8192³ grids covering radiation‑ and matter‑dominated epochs.
Networks form only when potential declines slower than field oscillation redshift.
Formed strings exhibit standard scaling consistent with velocity‑dependent one‑scale (VOS) model.
Numerical results closely match analytic VOS predictions for time‑dependent tension.

stari_mission_demonstration_of_in_space_.headline: NASA's STARI Mission Demonstrates First In‑Space Starlight Transfer
stari_mission_demonstration_of_in_space_.summary: The STARI two‑CubeSat demonstrator will relay a stellar beam between spacecraft up to 200 m apart, achieving diffraction‑limited fiber coupling in low Earth orbit.
highlights: Two 8U CubeSats will fly in formation with separations up to 200 m.
Differential GNSS, LED beacons and fast‑steering mirrors enable closed‑loop control of the starlight link.
The mission targets a 2029 launch to mature technologies for the proposed LIFE interferometer.

bennu_asteroid_organics.headline: Bennu asteroid amino acids reveal distinct solar‑system origins
bennu_asteroid_organics.summary: Researchers used intramolecular isotope analysis of beta‑alanine from Bennu and the Murchison meteorite to show the molecules formed in separate regions of the early solar system.
highlights: New pico‑CSIA and modified GC‑Orbitrap techniques measured carbon and nitrogen isotopes within individual beta‑alanine molecules.
The enriched carbon isotope in Bennu beta‑alanine is the highest ever recorded in an organic space molecule.
Average isotope values of Bennu and Murchison samples appear similar, but intramolecular patterns differ dramatically

the_mystery_of_how_hair_knows_where_to_g.headline: Chemotactic Self‑Organization Explains Mammalian Hair Follicle Patterns
the_mystery_of_how_hair_knows_where_to_g.summary: Researchers at University of Geneva showed that simple chemotactic interactions between cells can recreate the diverse hair follicle arrangements seen in mice and spiny mice.
highlights: A mathematical model of chemotaxis reproduces the follicle pattern of Mus musculus without invoking complex signaling cascades
The same model, adjusted for biochemical parameters, matches the highly regular pattern of Acomys dimidiatus
Findings challenge the long‑standing expansion‑induction theory that has dominated hair‑growth research for decades
Study published in PNAS (2026) demonstrates that variations in cell‑chemical interactions, not separate blueprints, drive

ozone_hole_growth_2026.headline: NASA Reports Antarctic Ozone Hole Expands to Decade‑High Size
ozone_hole_growth_2026.summary: In 2026 the Antarctic ozone hole grew to its seventh‑largest extent, covering about 10.5 million square miles due to an unusually strong polar vortex.
highlights: The hole reached a peak area of 10.5 million square miles (27.1 million km²) on September 18, 2026.
A powerful polar vortex kept the strongest winds several degrees from the South Pole, enlarging the depletion zone.
International controls under the Montreal Protocol prevented the hole from expanding an additional 1‑2 million square miles.
Measurements from NASA’s Aura satellite and NOAA’s Dobson Ozone Spectrophotometer recorded a low of 105 Dobson units over the

homo_naledi_all_female.headline: All-Female Burial Site Suggested for Homo naledi 240,000 Years Ago
homo_naledi_all_female.summary: Protein analysis of 23 teeth from at least 20 Homo naledi individuals found no male‑specific Amelogenin‑Y, hinting at an exclusively female burial.
highlights: Researchers recovered ancient proteins from Homo naledi tooth enamel using gentle acid‑etching.
No Amelogenin‑Y marker was detected in any of the 23 examined teeth.
The study examined the largest sample of Homo naledi individuals ever analyzed with proteomics.

iron_single_atom_catalyst_fenton.institution: Xinjiang Technical Institute of Physics and Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences
iron_single_atom_catalyst_fenton.headline: Core‑Shell Iron Single‑Atom Catalyst Achieves Near‑Complete 2,4‑DCP Removal
iron_single_atom_catalyst_fenton.summary: A SiO₂@Fe‑N‑C catalyst fabricated by XTIPC delivers 0.70 min⁻¹ degradation of 2,4‑DCP, reaching 95% removal in 20 minutes with minimal iron leaching.
highlights: Symmetric Fe‑N₄ sites bind reactants strongly while preserving electronic structure, unlike asymmetric Fe‑N₄O₂ sites.
The SiO₂@Fe‑N‑C catalyst retains the ordered mesoporous MCM‑41 structure after polymerization‑pyrolysis.
Pollutant‑removal efficiency stays above 95% over ten reuse cycles with negligible Fe leaching.
Hydroxyl radicals dominate the degradation pathway, achieving a mineralization efficiency of 62%.

2611_13115v1.headline: Unique CEMP-no Star in Sculptor Dwarf Galaxy Reveals Double Pop III Supernova Origins
2611_13115v1.summary: A high‑resolution VLT/UVES study of the metal‑poor star DR20080 in Sculptor shows unprecedented carbon enhancement and oxygen abundance, suggesting a faint Pop III supernova combined with a hypernova progenitor.
highlights: DR20080 has [Fe/H] = ‑3.26 and [C/Fe] = +1.60 after mixing corrections
Oxygen is unusually high at [O/Fe] = +1.53 compared to Milky Way CEMP‑no stars
Best‑fit models require a 43 M⊙ faint Pop III SN (E = 0.6×10^51 erg) plus a 19.4 M⊙ hypernova (E = 10×10^51 erg)
The star’s low [Ba/Fe] = ‑1.28 confirms its CEMP‑no classification

all_of_us_study_finds_thousands_of_new_g.headline: All of Us Study Uncovers Thousands of New Drug‑Response Genetic Variants
all_of_us_study_finds_thousands_of_new_g.summary: Analyzing nearly 100,000 diverse Americans, researchers identified thousands of novel variants in 16 pharmacogenes that could alter responses to common prescriptions.
highlights: Every participant carried at least one variant in the 16 studied pharmacogenes
One in four participants had taken a medication potentially affected by these variants
The diverse cohort revealed variants absent from earlier databases like the U.K. Biobank
Findings were published in Science Translational Medicine and highlight equity challenges in clinical implementation

dna_folding_single_cell_method.headline: Yale Researchers Unveil Epi-PHR Method Mapping DNA Folding and Epigenetic Marks in Single Cells
dna_folding_single_cell_method.summary: A new Yale technique called Epi-PHR simultaneously profiles 3D genome folding and epigenetic modifications in individual cells, offering unprecedented resolution for disease research.
highlights: Epi-PHR can map hundreds of genetic sites and multiple epigenetic marks within a single cell
The method uses hairpin‑shaped probes that emit fluorescence only when an epigenetic mark and a gene are spatially adjacent
Applied to a hippocampus slice, Epi-PHR revealed gradients of chromatin structure across neuronal populations

scientists_measure_gravitational_pull_be.headline: Physicists Measure Gravity Between 7.6 mg Silicon Wafers, New Small‑Scale Milestone
scientists_measure_gravitational_pull_be.summary: A team led by Shan‑Qing Yang at Sun Yat‑sen University measured a 471 attonewton pull between two 7.6 mg silicon wafers, confirming Newtonian gravity at unprecedentedly low masses.
highlights: The miniature torsion balance used deep silicon etching to create 7.6 mg test masses.
A rotating wheel with 16 silicon wafers generated a repeatable signal every 10 minutes.
Measured gravitational constant G with 5.3 percent uncertainty, matching the accepted value.

double_defense_photosynthesis_heat.headline: Dual Defense Boosts Photosystem II Heat Tolerance in Engineered Cyanobacteria
double_defense_photosynthesis_heat.summary: Researchers combined enhanced antioxidant enzymes and an oxidation‑resistant EF‑Tu variant to protect PSII, enabling Synechocystis cells to survive 46 °C heat stress.
highlights: Engineered Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 produced higher levels of SodB and VktA enzymes.
Modified EF‑Tu (C82S) remained functional despite oxidative stress.
At 46 °C the doubly enhanced strain maintained D1 synthesis at 1.6‑fold wild type levels.
Cells survived prolonged growth at 40 °C while wild‑type cells bleached and died.

gas_sensor_breath.institution: Hefei Institutes of Physical Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences
gas_sensor_breath.headline: New Sensor Detects Liver Disease Marker Dimethyl Sulfide in Breath
gas_sensor_breath.summary: A novel Pd–WO3 gas sensor with a CuO/Al2O3 filter can detect dimethyl sulfide down to 10 ppb in humid breath, enabling non‑invasive liver disease screening.
highlights: Response ratio for dimethyl sulfide versus hydrogen sulfide improved from 3.3 to 50.4.
Detection limit reached 10 ppb even at 90% relative humidity.
Filtering layer captures hydrogen sulfide while allowing dimethyl sulfide to pass.
Breath‑simulated tests showed reliable detection of disease‑related dimethyl sulfide levels.

fluoride_cognition_study.headline: Lifetime Fluoride Exposure Shows No Cognitive Decline in Irish Seniors
fluoride_cognition_study.summary: A study of about 2,500 Irish adults aged 65 found no association between decades of water fluoridation and later‑life cognitive performance.
highlights: ~2,500 participants from the Irish Longitudinal Study on Ageing were analyzed
Exposure groups were defined by residential fluoride levels since the 1964 national fluoridation rollout
Both mid‑life and early‑life fluoride exposure showed no link to cognitive test scores

supernova_impostor_binary.headline: Chandra Reveals Binary Companion Behind Repeating Outbursts of Supernova Impostor AT 2016blu
supernova_impostor_binary.summary: Astronomers used Chandra X‑ray observations to show that the luminous blue variable AT 2016blu in NGC 4559 is powered by a compact companion triggering 113‑day eruptions.
highlights: AT 2016blu, a ~33 M⊙ luminous blue variable, erupts every 113 days in NGC 4559 (~30 Mly away)
Chandra detected X‑ray brightening 100× higher during 2026 outbursts, unlike earlier archival data
The outbursts are best explained by an eccentric binary with a neutron star or black‑hole companion accreting transferred mass
XMM‑Newton and earlier Chandra pointings missed the source because of nearby ULX NGC 4559 X7
Researchers estimate ~2.7% of Earth’s mass is transferred each eruption

lumina_simulation.headline: Massive Lumina Simulation Illuminates Universe’s Rise from Cosmic Dark Age
lumina_simulation.summary: The new Lumina supercomputer run on Frontier models 2 billion years of early cosmic history, showing how stars, galaxies and black holes ended the dark age.
highlights: Lumina covers a 500 Mpc (≈1.6 billion light‑years) volume with half a trillion elements, 30× higher resolution than IllustrisTNG.
The simulation tracks both hydrogen and helium re‑ionization, attributing hydrogen ionization to early stars and galaxies and
Run on the Frontier supercomputer at Oak Ridge, using >100,000 CPU cores and ~15,000 GPUs, making it the largest

comet_organic_survival.headline: New Simulations Show Comets Unlikely Source of Earth’s Life‑Building Molecules
comet_organic_survival.summary: Computer models indicate comet impacts generally vaporize complex organics, making them an improbable delivery mechanism for the precursors of life on early Earth.
highlights: Simulations used hydrogen cyanide as a proxy for complex organics in comet impacts.
Impacts exceeding 15 km s⁻¹ (33,500 mph) or steep entry angles vaporize organics, leaving negligible residues.
Survival of organics would require a one‑in‑a‑million impact scenario.
Asteroid samples from OSIRIS‑REx’s Bennu contain RNA precursors, supporting asteroids over comets.

parker_solar_probe_turbulence.headline: Parker Solar Probe Finds Hidden Magnetic Reversal in Solar Wind Turbulence
parker_solar_probe_turbulence.summary: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe revealed that turbulent magnetic fields switch rotation direction at tiny scales, uncovering a hidden pattern in solar wind turbulence.
highlights: Magnetic fields rotate counter‑clockwise at large scales but clockwise at sub‑ion scales
The reversal becomes stronger and shifts to longer wavelengths farther from the Sun
First direct observation of a magnetic helicity sign change across the magnetohydrodynamic‑kinetic transition

ice_giants_magnetic_fields.headline: Ice Giants' Magnetic Fields May Shift Decades, New Study Shows
ice_giants_magnetic_fields.summary: New dynamo models suggest Uranus and Neptune's magnetic fields can vary dramatically over decades due to depth‑dependent electrical conductivity.
highlights: Uranus' field is tilted ~60° and offset from the planet’s center
Neptune’s field shows a similar tilt of ~47° and weaker intensity
Models predict non‑dipolar, non‑axisymmetric fields can change orientation by tens of degrees in just a few decades
Future JWST auroral observations aim to test these predicted variations

jwst_earliest_quasars_2026_11_12.headline: JWST Uncovers Earliest Known Quasar Pair Defying Black Hole Growth Models
jwst_earliest_quasars_2026_11_12.summary: Astronomers using JWST and Gemini North identified the quasar duo J1602+4228AB, seen 900 million years after the Big Bang, with black holes of 1.5 billion and 400 million solar masses.
highlights: The compact pair, nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, spans only 18,100 light‑years, about one‑fifth the Milky Way’s diameter.
Both supermassive black holes have masses of 1.5 billion and 400 million M☉, unprecedented for Cosmic Dawn.
Discovery came from JWST’s Aether survey using the NIRSpec IFU, which has catalogued 200 early‑universe quasars so far.
Results were published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, highlighting a gap in current black‑hole formation theories.

earth_s_fiery_birth_may_have_created_hun.headline: Hot Early Earth Could Have Synthesized Hundreds of Oceans of Water
earth_s_fiery_birth_may_have_created_hun.summary: Laboratory experiments show that iron‑oxide rocks reacting with hydrogen at 1,200‑1,400 °C can generate water fast enough to produce hundreds of oceans during Earth’s formation.
highlights: Rock samples lost up to 80% of iron oxide when heated in hydrogen, releasing water vapor
Experiments ran 15 minutes to three hours, demonstrating rapid water production
Calculations extrapolate the process could yield hundreds of oceans’ worth of water on the early Earth

euclid_data_release.headline: Euclid Telescope Releases First 3D Map of 900 Million Galaxies
euclid_data_release.summary: The ESA’s Euclid mission has unveiled its first major data release, cataloguing over 900 million galaxies and 60 million early‑universe light sources.
highlights: More than 15,000 strong gravitational‑lens (Einstein ring) candidates identified
1.7 million GB of spectra and imaging now available for 3‑D cosmic web reconstruction
Wide Survey covers 14% of the sky, with 85% of observations still pending

attosecond_xray_record_2026_11_12.headline: Record‑Intensity Attosecond Hard X‑Ray Pulses Achieved at European XFEL
attosecond_xray_record_2026_11_12.summary: Researchers at the European XFEL in Hamburg focused attosecond hard X‑ray pulses to 118.8 GW, reaching 2 × 10²⁰ W/cm² for ultrafast imaging.
highlights: Pulse intensity reached 118.8 GW on a 180 × 330 nm spot
Self‑chirping scheme produced hard X‑ray pulses with energies of several hundred microjoules
Advanced Kirkpatrick–Baez mirrors focused the pulses to record intensities
Team aims to use the source for nonlinear X‑ray experiments

amygdala_memory_role.headline: Amygdala Neurons Act as Memory Save Button, Study Finds
amygdala_memory_role.summary: Researchers recorded single amygdala neurons in epilepsy patients and found their activity predicts whether images are later remembered, suggesting a memory‑sorting role.
highlights: Single‑unit recordings from implanted electrodes identified amygdala neurons linked to later recall of images
Neurons showed category‑specific responses, with stronger initial firing increasing memory retention
Amygdala activity predicted memory better and faster than hippocampal neurons in the same patients

acs_prostate_screening_update_2026_11_12.headline: American Cancer Society Revises Prostate Cancer Screening Guidelines for Men
acs_prostate_screening_update_2026_11_12.summary: The ACS now advises biennial PSA testing from age 50 for average‑risk men and annual testing from age 45 for Black men and those with strong family histories.
highlights: Biennial PSA screening begins at age 50 for average‑risk men.
Annual PSA screening starts at age 45 for Black men and those with significant family history.
Guideline change aims to lower advanced‑stage diagnoses and mortality among Black patients.
Recommendation follows new evidence showing PSA screening reduces disease‑specific mortality in targeted groups.

ai_confirms_a_long_suspected_limit_on_qu.headline: AI Proves Decades‑Old Conjecture Limiting Quantum Computer Advantages
ai_confirms_a_long_suspected_limit_on_qu.summary: A team using Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 AI model has finally proved the Aaronson‑Ambainis conjecture, showing a class of random‑input problems offers no quantum speedup.
highlights: The proof was generated in about four days by the non‑public Fable 5.2 model and verified with Lean proof‑checking software.
Researchers at Physical Superintelligence, Stanford University, and University of Texas at Austin collaborated on the result.
The Aaronson‑Ambainis conjecture ruled out quantum speedup for decision problems with large random bit strings.
The finding narrows the search for quantum advantage to structured or non‑binary problems such as molecular simulation.

euclid_first_data_release.headline: Euclid Telescope Releases First Massive Dark Universe Data Set
euclid_first_data_release.summary: The ESA Euclid telescope unveiled DR1-Foundation, mapping over a billion objects and 15,000 lensing candidates, opening new avenues to probe dark matter and dark energy.
highlights: DR1-Foundation covers 13 months of observations across a sky area equivalent to 9,500 full moons
Catalogues include spectra from 160 million sources, 900 million galaxies and 60 million quasar candidates
15,000 strong gravitational lensing candidates will aid measurements of cosmic expansion
The release represents only 14% of Euclid’s planned six‑year survey, promising far more discoveries

basal_ganglia_map.headline: Scientists Release First Comprehensive Basal Ganglia Cell Map
basal_ganglia_map.summary: The international team cataloged over 25 million cells, revealing new neuron types linked to schizophrenia and other psychiatric disorders, and demonstrating targeted gene therapy in Parkinson’s models.
highlights: More than 25 million cells were profiled to create a detailed parts list of basal ganglia cell types.
A previously unknown neuron type associated with schizophrenia was identified.
Cell types implicated in depression, bipolar disorder, and post‑traumatic stress disorder were mapped.
Gene therapy targeting a specific basal ganglia cell subset proved as effective and safer than a blanket approach in mouse

bennu_sample_isotopes.headline: Bennu Sample Reveals Intramolecular Isotope Shock in β‑Alanine
bennu_sample_isotopes.summary: New isotope analyses of β‑alanine from NASA’s OSIRIS‑REx Bennu sample show striking carbon‑13 differences compared to the Murchison meteorite, hinting at diverse early‑Solar‑System chemistry.
highlights: β‑alanine isotopic ratios differ between neighboring carbon atoms in the Bennu sample
The same molecule from the Murchison meteorite shows a contrasting intramolecular carbon‑13 pattern
Measurements were made with Penn State’s pico‑CSIA and a modified GC‑Orbitrap mass spectrometer
Findings suggest the molecule formed in distinct regions of the protoplanetary disk

euclid_dr1_2026.headline: Euclid Releases First Massive Data Set, Paving Way for 3D Sky Map
euclid_dr1_2026.summary: The ESA Euclid telescope’s DR1‑Foundation release maps 1900 sq deg, cataloguing over one billion objects to advance dark energy and dark matter studies.
highlights: DR1‑Foundation covers an area equivalent to about 9,500 full moons.
The Wide and Deep Surveys together represent roughly 14% of Euclid’s six‑year mission sky coverage.
Euclid’s space‑based observations avoid atmospheric interference, offering higher resolution than ground‑based DESI.

chinese_scientists_cool_atoms_near_absol.institution: Chinese Academy of Sciences / Tiangong Space Station
chinese_scientists_cool_atoms_near_absol.headline: Chinese Tiangong Achieves Record‑Low 10 Picokelvin Temperature in Space
chinese_scientists_cool_atoms_near_absol.summary: Using optical‑dipole traps on the Tiangong space station, researchers cooled 20,000 rubidium atoms to 10 picokelvins, the coldest temperature ever measured.
highlights: Optical‑dipole trap (ODT) held 20,000 rubidium atoms in microgravity
Temperature reached 10 picokelvins, surpassing previous 52 picokelvin ISS record
Result published in Science and may enable quantum‑simulation experiments in space

protein_aging_review.headline: Large Review Finds Lower Protein May Slow Biological Aging
protein_aging_review.summary: A review of 361 studies suggests that reducing dietary protein could decelerate biological aging by improving metabolic health and lowering inflammation.
highlights: Analysis of 361 studies links protein restriction to slower aging markers in animals and humans.
Lower protein intake reduces inflammation and boosts fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) levels.
Benefits depend on activity level; active individuals may still need higher protein for muscle maintenance.
Researchers propose personalized protein guidelines based on age and exercise.

solar_storm_atmosphere_contribution.headline: Earth’s Atmosphere Dominated Ions in Record‑Breaking May 2024 Solar Superstorm
solar_storm_atmosphere_contribution.summary: In May 2024 a massive geomagnetic storm revealed that about 85% of ring‑current ions came from Earth’s ionosphere, weakening the magnetic field by roughly 40%.
highlights: Arase satellite (JAXA) measured ~85% oxygen ions from Earth’s upper atmosphere during the storm
Magnetic field intensity dropped 40% at ~16,000 km altitude, the strongest near‑Earth weakening recorded
SYM‑H index fell to −518 nT, the second‑largest disturbance since 1981

early_earth_oxygen_sponge_crystals.headline: Ancient Zircons Reveal Earth’s Mantle Soaked Up Oxygen 3.4 Billion Years Ago
early_earth_oxygen_sponge_crystals.summary: New Nature Geoscience study shows mantle began absorbing cyanobacterial oxygen around 3.4 billion years ago, over a billion years before the Great Oxidation Event.
highlights: Zircon crystals from sanukitoid rocks record oxidation states via apatite inclusions
Oxygen uptake in the mantle intensified between 3.4 billion and 3 billion years ago
Study dates mantle‑oxygen interaction to ~3.4 billion years, far earlier than previous estimates
Only 14 sanukitoid samples yielded 72 zircons and 39 apatite inclusions, highlighting data scarcity

viral_infection_hidden_damage_vaccine_pr.headline: Vaccines Shield Against Hidden Immune Damage After Viral Infections, Study Finds
viral_infection_hidden_damage_vaccine_pr.summary: A mouse study shows that acute viral infections cause lasting spleen fibrosis and weakened T‑cell responses, but prior vaccination fully prevents these immune impairments.
highlights: Acute viral infection induced splenic fibrosis and disrupted immune‑cell architecture in mice.
Affected mice displayed reduced de novo T‑cell activation and poorer responses to new challenges.
Mice vaccinated before infection retained normal spleen structure and T‑cell function, avoiding immune deficits.
Findings published in Cell Death & Disease (2026) by researchers from Universitat Pompeu Fabra.

ai_agents_collider_calculations.headline: AI Agents Accelerate Collider Calculations, Cutting Runtime Up to 805‑Fold
ai_agents_collider_calculations.summary: Researchers at University of Cambridge show large‑language models can self‑evolve algorithms that compute tree‑level scattering amplitudes up to 805 times faster.
highlights: OpenAI’s Codex generates candidate programs evaluated for correctness and efficiency.
Optimizing for scaling yielded an algorithm whose cost grows linearly with particle number, 805× faster than the seed.
Complexity‑focused search reduced arithmetic operations by a factor of 48.

brain_it_ai_visual_patterns.headline: Brain‑IT AI Reconstructs Seen Images from fMRI Scans with High Accuracy
brain_it_ai_visual_patterns.summary: A new AI system called Brain‑IT uses fMRI data from the visual cortex to predict both layout and semantic content, generating pictures that closely match what participants viewed.
highlights: Brain‑IT surpasses previous reconstruction methods on standard objective metrics
Accurate images are produced with only one hour of fMRI data, compared to earlier models needing 40 hours
The system builds on the Universal Brain Encoder, which learns voxel‑level representations across participants
Predictions are refined by an off‑the‑shelf diffusion generator trained on massive image datasets
Researchers are exploring EEG as a simpler alternative to fMRI for future versions

sunlight_quantum_clock_2026.headline: First Quantum Clock Powered by Sunlight Opens New Astronomical Possibilities
sunlight_quantum_clock_2026.summary: Researchers at University of Colorado Boulder have built the first optical clock that locks to solar‑induced iron transitions, enabling novel stellar velocity measurements.
highlights: The clock uses a frequency comb to translate sunlight‑derived spectral lines into precise time ticks
During the 2024 partial solar eclipse the device detected a measurable spectral shift caused by the Moon
Potential applications include probing solar eruptions, sunspots, and detecting exoplanet‑induced Doppler shifts
Piet Schmidt of the National Metrology Institute of Germany notes the design showcases a star‑based optical clock concept

lofar_deep_image.headline: LOFAR Delivers Deepest Low‑Frequency Radio Image, Revealing 63,000 Sources
lofar_deep_image.summary: An international team led by Leiden University used LOFAR to capture a 400‑TB, 8‑billion‑pixel image of ELAIS‑N1, unveiling 63,000 radio sources.
highlights: 200 hours of observation produced an 8‑billion‑pixel map covering 400 TB of data
Spider platform at SURF processed the dataset in months, cutting processing time tenfold
The image resolves filaments and jets around active galactic nuclei and young star‑forming galaxies

southern_ocean_deep_sea_discoveries.headline: National Geographic Documentary Shows Young Oceanographers Tackling Climate Crisis
southern_ocean_deep_sea_discoveries.summary: The new National Geographic film follows researchers from the Southern Ocean to West Africa, showcasing innovative tools and community‑driven projects to combat ocean warming.
highlights: Andrew Thurber’s team discovers the southernmost hydrothermal vent using the ROV SuBastian, revealing swarms of pregnant female
Maiyai Taal Hocheimy’s GREAT Institute trains Gambian youth to protect mangroves that could buffer sea‑level rise in Banjul.
Katy Croff Bell’s Ocean Discovery League pilots the low‑cost DORIS system, imaging depths of 6,000 m for under $10,000.

hidden_brain_signals_alzheimers.headline: Stanford Team Uncovers Hidden Brain Signals Predicting Alzheimer’s Years Early
hidden_brain_signals_alzheimers.summary: Researchers identified resting‑state fMRI patterns that forecast Alzheimer’s risk up to 12 years before symptoms, outperforming traditional biomarkers in.
highlights: ARC score distinguished super agers from Alzheimer’s patients with ~85% accuracy using resting‑state fMRI.
In 1,300 adults aged 55‑70, higher ARC scores predicted faster cognitive decline and amyloid‑beta accumulation over up to 12
ARC outperformed demographic, genetic, amyloid‑beta and tau markers, and combined use further improved prediction.
Researchers propose targeting the identified connectivity patterns with cognitive training or transcranial magnetic stimulation.

ancient_egypt_skulls.headline: Ancient Egyptian Royal Attendants Show Evidence of Fatal Head Injuries
ancient_egypt_skulls.summary: Forensic analysis of 46 Abydos skulls reveals that about 39% suffered lethal head trauma, supporting a centuries‑old theory of retainer sacrifice.
highlights: 46 skulls from the First Dynasty were re‑examined using modern forensic methods
18 crania displayed linear fractures and sharp‑force injuries consistent with perimortem blows
The study was published in Frontiers in Environmental Archaeology and led by Dr. Roselyn Campbell of Purdue University
